(1) **Home AND work fall out of `lat`/`lng`/`ts` alone**, no model and no API: time-weighted night share (01–05) against weekday-working-window share (Mon–Fri 09–18) separates them cleanly for FOUR of the seven (a work cluster carrying 0.0 night hours), and the other three fail in three DISTINCT ways — `aaron_larsen` ambiguous (one cell carrying 25.5 night h and 24.9 working-window h), `delia_lindberg` working from home, `avery_walsh` yielding no work cluster at all — which is why the result is three-state rather than a boolean. §6 predicted the home rule and it holds; **workplace detection is new**, §6 never named it. §6's R≈150 m is tightened to 120 m (~2.4× the measured 50 m median accuracy) but is INHERITED, not measured — eleven days cannot validate a stay radius, and design/27 §7.1 records it as needing revalidation rather than pretending it settled. (2) **THE correctness invariant §6 could not have known: the cadence is adaptive, so counting fixes counts the sampler.** Measured gaps p50 45 s / p90 1,794 s confirm the 1800 s still-ceiling, and driving is 56.9% of FIXES but **10.2% of TIME** — a count-weighted statistic over this table is wrong by 5.6×. Every derived figure passes through one `dwell = min(next_ts - ts, 1900 s)` function in `nora/domain/mobility.py`, in exactly one place, so no consumer can get it wrong independently. (3) **Neutrality is a GATE.** The operator's constraint was that the substrate serve neither agent nor app but sit under both; a neutrality claim living only in a comment is decoration, so it is a `forbidden` import contract — `nora.analytics` and `nora.domain.mobility` may not import `nora.agent`/`app`/`platform`/`tag`/`doctrine`/`ingest`/`engagement`/`skills`, and `lint-imports` turns red on the first reach-back. It follows that the substrate carries **no disclosure metadata at all** — no `disclosable_to`, no audience column; R-21/R-31 gate in the agent and session auth gates in the app, each consumer at its own edge. «Internal-only at first» is therefore not a flag but simply the absence of consumers, which is a stronger thing to hold true. (4) **Labelling is fail-closed, R-27's shape falling out of the algorithm rather than bolted on:** `home` / `work` / **`unlabeled`**, never a guess — `aaron_larsen` (25.5 night h AND 24.9 working-window h at one cell) will come back `unlabeled`, the correct answer that will look like a gap. Life360's saved labels are a naming HINT and never the authority, since `blake_lindqvist`'s own home cluster carries another household's name. **AMENDED 2026-09-17 (design/27 §3.7, DEC-190, ADR 0014):** this is REVERSED for identity and name and UPHELD for geometry. A tagged place's stable id and name now outrank an auto-identified one; its coordinates never do (a work pin in this corpus sits 636 m from the cluster it names). Point (4)'s fail-closed three-state labelling is unchanged, but it now labels a place that already exists rather than deciding whether one exists. **(4b) `person_id` IS MUTABLE and the substrate must not key on it (operator, 2026-08-18).** `clara_yates`→`clara_lawson` split one continuous track into two identities INSIDE this corpus — and the damage is not cosmetic: her working-window workplace dwell was 31.4 h + 11.7 h as two people against
43.1 h merged (44.2 h is her broader all-hours total at that cell, not a third
figure), and `min_weekdays = 3` can fail the smaller fragment, so **a rename silently downgrades a correct `work` label to `unlabeled`**. Fail-closed stops a wrong assertion; it does NOT stop losing a right one. Derivation therefore groups on a `subject_id` resolved from identity at the composition root, `person_id` retained for provenance — and the merge is DECLARED, never inferred, because auto-merging two people who genuinely share a home is worse than leaving them split (undeclared candidates raise `nora_analytics_unmerged_candidates_total`). | DEC-124 | **Every person-scoped tool's disclosure model is TWO axes, uniform across the whole platform, and neither is tunable per tool or per data category — stated here as a general rule for the first time, generalizing what `where_is` already does (DEC-54, DEC-59, R-31/R-47) rather than inventing anything new.** Operator, 2026-08-20, restated after it had already been settled once: "whoever is the identified person can use all of the information or all of the tools that are whitelisted, and any of the unidentified require a guard" — and, made concrete, "whoever gets into the Discord group or Signal group where Nora exists is, to be honest, trusted or known." Written down now because the question of whether a NEW kind of derived data (presence rhythm/anomaly/routes, Tier 3/5) needs its own bespoke disclosure design kept resurfacing — it does not, and this entry exists so it stops resurfacing. **Axis 1 — the FEATURE FLAG: is this capability even switched on for this room, at all.** A per-conversation `policy.toml` field, `location = true`'s own shape — an operator/product decision, one boolean per capability per room, orthogonal to who is currently present. A new tool needing its own on/off control per room gets a new field of this same shape; it does not get a new SAFEGUARD. **Axis 2 — the SAFEGUARD: is everyone currently in this room a known, identified person.** `DisclosureGuard` (`nora.agent.whereis`) intersects `RoomView`'s current membership against the mapped roster and refuses — not omits, not degrades — the instant any member is unmapped, fail-closed on a degraded/unreadable roster too (DEC-54). This is the SAME check for every tool and every data category; it does not get stricter for a more sensitive derived fact (rhythm, an inferred pattern) or looser for a less sensitive one (a saved place's name, R-35's deliberate inverse for a different reason — the guarded thing there is the ENTRY's existence, not the audience). Operationally, "identified" already collapses to "is a member of the actual Signal/Discord group Nora is deployed in": every person in those groups is mapped in `identity.toml` and listed in that room's `policy.toml` roster by construction, because the operator only ever adds real friends to them — so the roster check and "did a stranger just join this room" are the same event, not two systems that could disagree. **What this settles for P1 (Nora tools reading the presence-analytics substrate, issue #9) and any future person-scoped tool, before it is built:** reuse `DisclosureGuard` as-is for axis 2 — do not design a new privacy tier per derived-data kind. Axis 1 is the only per-tool decision, and it is a naming/scoping question (one flag for all of presence, or one per tier), not a security one. `DisclosureGuard` currently lives inside `nora/agent/whereis.py`, coupled to a module named after its first caller — moving it to a shared location (e.g. `nora/agent/disclosure.py`) is a housekeeping step for whoever builds the first tool that imports it from outside `whereis`, not a design decision this entry needs to make. | `RULE_TESTS["R-31"]`, `tests/test_whereis.py::test_whereis_refuses_to_disclose_outside_the_circle`, `::test_whereis_discloses_nothing_on_a_degraded_room_it_cannot_verify`, `tests/test_whereis.py::test_a_circle_member_who_is_not_in_the_room_can_still_be_asked_about` (R-47) — the existing enforcement for `where_is`, the one instance this entry generalizes; a future tool reusing `DisclosureGuard` inherits these guarantees by construction and does not need a new test proving the guard itself works, only that it called it |

| DEC-127 | **Trip settlement — Tier 5's `extract_trips` protected only the trip-to-stay boundary (`open_stay_started_ts`), never a trip's own trailing edge during continuous movement, and that gap is what fragmented a real drive in production (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-trip-settlement-design.md`).** Live evidence, not a hypothetical: within 20 minutes of Tier 5 (DEC-122) deploying, Aaron Novak's one continuous ~20-minute/15+km highway drive (18:10–18:29 HKT) came out as six `presence_trips` rows, because `_tick`'s ~120s cadence handed `run_once` a fresh batch every cycle and the final, unconditional flush — `if len(buffer) >= min_trip_fixes: trips.append(...)` — turned whatever sat in the buffer at batch-end into a finished trip regardless of whether the drive was still going. Stays never had this problem because their equivalent guard (`open_stay_started_ts`) lives inside `segment_stays` itself, one layer below `_tick`'s cadence; trips had no analogous guard at all. **The fix: `is_driving`, Life360's own per-fix motion signal (100% filled, unlike `speed_kmh`'s 14.7%), as the primary settlement signal, `settled_seconds` as a time-based fallback when it is `None`, and the watermark holding back an undecided trailing group instead of consuming it** — the same `corridor_id IS NULL` "don't consume yet" shape DEC-122's own corridor accumulation already established. **Two real bugs surfaced during implementation, not just at design time, and both are part of what shipped.** (1) `segment_stays` always returns a non-`None` `open_stay` for any non-empty chunk — even a single fix mid-drive trivially forms a degenerate one-point "stay" — so the plan's original wiring (gate on `open_stay_started_ts`) would have been a no-op; the actual fix needed a new discriminator in `run_once` that only treats the final chunk's trailing group as genuinely undecided when `chunk[-1].is_driving is True`, or (2) below, when `is_driving is None`, the group hasn't yet dwelled past `stay_min_dwell_seconds`, AND `settled_seconds` has not yet elapsed since the tail fix (the third conjunct `tail_is_movement` also requires, via `trailing_fix_is_settled`) — otherwise existing behavior is unchanged. (2) A naive `is_driving = None` fallback wired as pure elapsed-time-against-`settled_seconds` would have shipped something WORSE than the original bug: Life360's ~10-minute resting cadence is short enough relative to `settled_seconds` (900s) that a stationary subject's trailing group's last-fix timestamp keeps refreshing before the clock can elapse, so it never settles that way — measured at 41 phantom zero-distance trips in a 12-trip test scenario before this was caught. The fix is a SECOND, `None`-only gate: a trailing group with `is_driving=None` that has already dwelled past `stay_min_dwell_seconds` is treated as the stay-in-progress it looks like — deliberately never applied when `is_driving` is actually `True`, because a real driving signal must always beat the spatial-dwell proxy (a genuinely gridlocked driver must not be wrongly treated as arrived). **Only gate (1) is literally shared code**: `nora.domain.mobility.trailing_fix_is_settled` (signature `(last, *, now_ms, settled_seconds)` — no dwell parameter) implements just the `is_driving`/`settled_seconds` check, and both `extract_trips` and `run_once` call that same function, so the two callers cannot disagree on THAT check specifically. Gate (2), the dwell check, is a separate inline computation that exists only in `run_once` (`nora/analytics/rollup.py`'s `tail_dwelled`) — `extract_trips` never calls it and has no knowledge it exists; `extract_trips` only ever sees the ALREADY-RESOLVED `open_stay_started_ts` that `run_once` hands it after `run_once` itself has combined both gates. So the two functions cannot disagree on the FINAL outcome (which fixes are trip-eligible) even though gate (2) itself is not shared code — the sharing is at the predicate for gate (1) and at the resolved boundary for gate (2), not at one shared function for both. **`max_trip_duration_seconds` (default 10800/3h) is the safety valve against a stuck `is_driving=True` signal** — named explicitly as a judgment call, not a measured value, since no genuine multi-hour trip exists in production yet to measure against; the interaction between a stuck-`True` signal held "parked" by the discriminator above and this cap firing to force settlement was checked with a dedicated probe (`test_a_stuck_is_driving_signal_is_force_settled_by_the_cap`), not merely assumed to compose correctly. **Verified past self-attestation**: multiple independent rounds of mutation testing rebuilt the pre-fix fragmentation bug from scratch twice and independently reproduced the resting-fixes phantom-trip bug by reverting the dwell gate, each time confirming the test suite actually goes red. Corrected end-to-end numbers, the same 6-day/2-commute simulation DEC-122 already used: 12 trips / 2 corridors under the shipped fix, versus 60 trips / 10 corridors under the original fragmented behavior, versus 53 trips / 41 phantoms under the fix round's own first, rejected naive attempt. **Two things are carried forward as named open items, not silently dropped.** First, the watermark-holdback mechanism has its own real (if bounded) limit, and it presupposes fixes keep arriving throughout — the backlog can only grow while new fixes land; a batch with genuinely zero new fixes never touches it at all (`run_once`'s own `if fixes:` guard skips it entirely). With that precondition, a subject who keeps generating fixes but whose trailing group keeps re-qualifying as undecided holds the watermark frozen until the accumulating backlog crosses `backfill_threshold` — real defaults `batch_limit=400`/`backfill_threshold=4000` put the bound at roughly `backfill_threshold × fix_cadence`, on the order of 11 hours at a realistic ~10s *driving* cadence — self-healing once the wider backfill batch arrives, but a real stall, not a "safe" full stop (design spec §2.3). A device that goes dark instead — no fixes arriving at all — is a different, genuinely unbounded stall that this bound does not describe; it self-heals once fixes resume, via the existing chunk-gap split, not via this backlog mechanism. Second, `last_cluster_id` — DEC-115's place-clustering dirty-set marker (`cluster_places`'s own gate; unrelated to corridor clustering, which has no watermark column at all and instead uses `presence_trips.corridor_id IS NULL`, DEC-122) — is not held back alongside this fix's watermark; assessed as benign, because `cluster_places`'s gate (`fixes[-1].id > last_cluster_id`) opens on ANY new fix arriving this cycle, whether held back by this branch's trip-settlement logic or not, so place clustering never runs less often after this change than it did before. The only skip window is a cycle with genuinely no new fixes at all, which cannot close a place-forming stay that wasn't already closeable. **Out of scope, stated rather than silently dropped:** whether `segment_stays`'s own open-stay mechanism has an analogous cross-tick timing gap for a stay's arrival time (flagged, not confirmed as a bug — Tier 1 is live 13 days and reviewed thoroughly, this investigation was partial); and the 9 trip rows already fragmented in production before this fix, which are not backfilled or re-derived — new drives from deploy onward extract correctly, the existing rows stay as they are. | `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-trip-settlement-design.md`; `tests/unit/test_mobility.py` (`test_a_trailing_group_still_driving_is_held_back_not_finalized`, `test_a_trailing_group_no_longer_driving_settles_immediately`, `test_is_driving_none_falls_back_to_the_settled_seconds_clock`, `test_max_trip_duration_forces_settlement_even_while_still_driving`, `test_a_real_open_stay_boundary_bypasses_settlement_entirely`, `test_a_held_back_group_below_min_trip_fixes_is_still_held_not_dropped`); `tests/unit/test_analytics_rollup.py` (`test_a_continuous_drive_across_many_ticks_settles_into_one_trip`, `test_a_stuck_is_driving_signal_is_force_settled_by_the_cap`, `test_a_parked_tail_with_is_driving_false_is_still_an_open_stay`, `test_a_drive_with_no_is_driving_signal_waits_for_settled_seconds`, `test_a_resting_tail_with_no_signal_does_not_stall_the_watermark`, `test_a_gridlocked_drive_never_writes_a_stay_while_the_tail_is_still_movement`, `test_a_repeating_commute_actually_grows_corridors_over_days`) **NOT ENFORCED for the files named above that were deleted in the 2026-10 PII scrub** (they held real locations and names; deleted, not repointed, because there is nothing to repoint at). Recorded rather than silently dropped. |

| DEC-130 | **The Dreamer's write boundary is a two-verb port with no delete, and its supersession names a successor that is nullable AT THE PORT and strict at each implementation (`nora/domain/ports.py`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-20-dreamer-substrate-plan.md` Task 2.2).** `DreamSink` exposes exactly `propose` and `supersede`. **There is no delete verb, on the port or on any implementation** — «invalidate, never delete» enforced by the type rather than by every author remembering it, checked on the Protocol itself so one test fails for every implementation at once; a single opaque `write(result)` was rejected for the opposite reason, that it cannot express supersede at all and would lose the new-vs-replaces distinction at the boundary. **`propose(key, ())` is R-27's three states expressed in the port:** an empty tuple is `nothing_found` («I looked and there was nothing»), reaches the sink, and is where `LanguageConsolidator`'s time-driven rescore lives — the decay that fades a dormant room arrives with `lag == 0` and none of the five adaptor fields has a slot for it; NOT calling `propose` is `unavailable` («I could not check»). Collapsing the two silently drops decay and turns a wiring gap into a false negative. **`propose` returns ids, not a count**, because `supersede` must be able to name what a previous `propose` produced; `now_ms` is on the verb rather than on `Proposal` because one tick writes many proposals at one instant and per-proposal clocks invite a batch whose rows disagree about when the batch happened. **`payload: object` and `replaced_by: str | None` are the same decision twice.** Provenance (`instruction_sha256`, `model`, `established_by`) rides on `Proposal` rather than inside `payload` so the runtime never names an adaptor's value type; and `replaced_by` is nullable because two tiers derived the need for a successor field from different specs — the fact tier, whose supersessions always have one (a contradicted fact is replaced by the corrected one, hence its `(superseded_by is null) = (superseded_at is null)` biconditional), and the note tier, whose `retire` case has none (an anchor date passed; a dinner that happened is not replaced by anything). A non-nullable field would force the second tier to mint a placeholder id to satisfy the signature — the invent-a-value-to-satisfy-a-schema move forbidden elsewhere — so the port stays permissive and each sink is strict: **a port that hard-codes one tier's cardinality is the same mistake as a `payload` typed to one tier's value.** `source` is a **warrant** (a URL or equivalent pointer to evidence) and never a row id, which is why the successor is its own field rather than smuggled through it; that also keeps `because` narrow enough to stay a constrained enum on the implementing side instead of becoming free text carrying a UUID. Six decisions. **(1) The hard line is a property of the runtime, not a setting.** A background process that can speak to the group unprompted — or set a reminder, or write to the events store — with nobody waiting on it is a categorically different thing from one that can only read. `NativeTool` gains `read_only` and `ToolRegistry.read_only_tools()` derives the Dreamer's CEILING from it. **The argument for deriving it is the list it replaces:** the keystone's §4 hand-named six act verbs and was FOUR SHORT — the events family (DEC-117) joined the table after that list was written — so a plan copying it verbatim would have handed a background agent four write verbs. A unit-keyed adaptor is narrowed again to `UNIT_SAFE_TOOLS`: every other read tool is bound to ONE conversation's roster and record, and a unit has no room to bind them to — binding one to an arbitrary room of that unit would be an R-31 disclosure decision nobody has made, so it is refused rather than guessed at. The cost is named: the fact adjudicator researches the open web and cannot read the group's own transcript. **(3) `create_agent` cannot build it, and no spec said so.** It requires a `ReplyGuard` — a deliverer, terminal verbs, the `tool_choice` relaxation — and `create_model_provider` hardcoded `tool_choice="required"`, under which a loop with NO terminal verb can never stop by itself: the guard's `BeforeModelCallEvent` hook is the only thing that ends a turn and it ends it by observing a terminal call (DEC-21/DEC-32). So: `DreamGuard` (R-7 default-deny and the per-tool ceiling, no deliverer, no terminality, no `tool_choice` relaxation, and it registers NO model-call hook — it must not have the power to end a turn), and `tool_choice` becomes a field on `ModelSpec` rather than only a parameter on `create_model_provider`, because `ModelSource` is what actually builds the provider and it built every one from the tag path's value. **(4) R-27 at the run, and the mapping is the point.** `DreamOutcome` is `ok` / `nothing_found` / `unavailable`. A model response that will not parse is `unavailable` («this batch was never actually read»), never `nothing_found` — because the caller must not advance a watermark past a batch nobody read. That is `ExtractionUnparseableError`'s guarantee expressed as a value now that the adaptor contract returns one instead of raising. A well-formed EMPTY return is `nothing_found` and still calls `commit(key, ())`, which is where time-driven decay lives. **(5) Screening moved EARLIER than the plan put it** — onto the model's raw envelope items, before any tier type exists. Screening a parsed value would need every adaptor to expose its own text for inspection, which is one more surface a tier can forget; an item is generic, sees fields the typed parse drops, and still drops at item granularity so one poisoned item never costs its siblings. `scan_identifiers`, never `scan_reply`: the latter's model-name half matches nine ordinary English words and would silently delete legitimate lexemes. **Amended 2026-09-28 by DEC-230** (`design/cognition-loop` step 0): the memo body's `Kept` section is narrowed OUT of this clause's screen — it may hold a password verbatim by design (`12-schemas.md` §3, D5) and renders normally; every other write verb's envelope item is still screened here, unchanged. **(6) Per-adaptor isolation, and the backoff key moved WITH it** (gate D3). Ships inert: `[dreamer] enabled = false`, no adaptor migrated, `dream_loop` with an empty adaptor tuple byte-for-byte the loop carrying live traffic. | R-70 | **Standing's whole slot hold is a STARTUP GATE, never a comment, and every wait it makes is inside it.** `[standing] timeout_seconds + 4 x [standing] store_timeout_seconds <= [standing] max_slot_hold_seconds` (4 since 2026-09-24, when note proposals left the debrief), refused at boot by `Config._the_standing_slot_hold_fits_its_budget`; and `[standing] window <= [store] context_window`, refused by its sibling, because the debrief folds `ctx.transcript` and a larger value silently selects the same rows. **Neither is gated on `enabled`** — a number that lies is wrong on the page whether or not it is running, and switch-on is the worst moment to discover it. | R-71 | **DEPRECATED 2026-09-24 — the per-turn `TurnVerdict`, its port, both stores and their contract suite were deleted with the debrief's grounding verdict (`design/standing-compact/`). The row is kept, unrenumbered, as a record; it no longer describes anything that runs.** **A `TurnVerdict` is written ONCE per turn and never rewritten, and that is enforced by the SCHEMA rather than by convention** — `tag_id` is the PRIMARY KEY and `SqlTurnVerdictStore` has only `save`, a plain INSERT with no `ON CONFLICT` and no update verb on the port at all (26 §3, the shape `DreamSink`'s missing delete already uses). A second verdict for one turn is a duplicate-key error, because it means the turn was debriefed TWICE and silently overwriting would hide that. **The split from `Standing` is structural, not stylistic**: it was found by a bug — per-turn fields lived on the per-conversation row, so the re-derivation trigger read a `grounded` flag the NEXT TURN had already overwritten, and a per-turn fact on a row revised every turn is a fact with a lifetime of one turn. **A verdict failure never costs the position**: the position is what the next turn reads, the verdict is read by a re-derivation pass that does not exist yet, so the verdict is written AFTER and its failure rides on its own counter. | R-72 | **DEPRECATED 2026-09-24 — both re-derivation triggers (the ungrounded verdict and the `[standing] rebuild_after_folds` ceiling) and the code's use of `Standing.consumed_verdict_tag` (the column stays in the schema) were deleted with the debrief's grounding verdict (`design/standing-compact/`). The row is kept, unrenumbered, as a record; it no longer describes anything that runs.** **A position is REBUILT rather than revised when the previous turn's verdict says it was not grounded, or when `fold_count` reaches `[standing] rebuild_after_folds` — and `ungrounded` wins whenever both hold** (26 §4/S2). The ordering is the MEASUREMENT, not a preference: §6 reads `nora_standing_rederivations_total{trigger}` to ask whether the trigger has degraded into «a clock wearing a condition», so labelling a turn that actually went wrong as `ceiling` manufactures that exact false reading. Three further constraints, each falsified by mutation: the prior is **discarded at the RENDER, never at the read**, because 26 §4's non-negotiable is that the fold READS it and `nora_debrief_prior_total` must stay able to tell a re-derived turn from one that could not read; `fold_count` **resets to 1** on a rebuild, or the ceiling latches on and fires forever; and `prior is None` is **never** a re-derivation, because the first fold of a conversation builds from the window regardless and counting it would drown the signal. An unreadable verdict store does not rebuild ON THE UNGROUNDED CONDITION — R-27's «I could not check» must not cost a position because an instrument was down — but the CEILING is still evaluated, because `fold_count` is on the row already in hand and needs no second store. The unqualified claim was false and the named test only ever exercised the below-ceiling half. **The ungrounded condition is keyed on an ACTED-ON WATERMARK — `standing.consumed_verdict_ms`, migration 0037 — never on a timestamp comparison.** `latest` answers the newest verdict of any age and a verdict is written only when a fold fully succeeds, so with no guard at all one ungrounded verdict latched the trigger ON: three consecutive rebuilds with `fold_count` pinned at 1, while the metric §6 reads for degradation reported the trigger as healthy. **Two comparisons were tried as the remedy and both were wrong.** `created_at > prior.updated_at` was dead on arrival — one `now_ms` per turn stamps the position and the verdict identically, so `>` refused the only sequence it existed for and the counter read flat zero, which §6 reads as the trigger having degraded into a clock. `created_at >= prior.updated_at` fixed that and remained a PROXY: `updated_at` stands in for «a rebuild consumed this verdict», and any proxy is falsifiable by a path that moves it without doing the thing. That path is ordinary — `latest` fails for ONE turn, the trigger correctly declines (R-27), the fold revises and advances `updated_at` past the verdict, and the comparison is false forever. The ungrounded verdict is not deferred, it is gone: «I could not check» converted into «there was nothing», permanently, measured over three turns. **And the READ is ungrounded-only** (`TurnVerdictStore.latest_ungrounded`, which replaced a `latest` of either kind rather than joining it). The watermark alone did not close the drop: a read answering the newest verdict of ANY kind lets a later GROUNDED verdict bury an older unconsumed ungrounded one, and the burying turn is the ordinary shape of a successful fold following one where the read failed — 0 re-derivations, watermark still null, the verdict still in the store, measured over three turns. The wrong read is made unrepresentable rather than documented, the same move the port already makes by having no `write`; `idx_turn_verdict_ungrounded` had existed for exactly this query and was serving nothing. So the property is RECORDED: the row carries the `tag_id` of the verdict a re-derivation acted on — the verdict's IDENTITY, not its `created_at`, because a timestamp is a third proxy: two ungrounded verdicts sharing a millisecond collapse to one watermark value and the second is never acted on, and this codebase already asserts that premise twice in the tie-breaks both `latest_ungrounded` implementations use. **And the read must actually reach its index**: `.is_(False)` renders `grounded IS false` while `idx_turn_verdict_ungrounded` is created `WHERE (grounded = false)`, which the planner cannot prove equivalent — so every fold sequentially scanned the whole verdict table inside the held lock while the docstring four lines up claimed the index served it. The ANSWER was correct throughout, which is why a green gate and two reviews missed it; the enforcing test asserts the PLAN rather than the spelling, because a spelling test would pin today's fix instead of the property, advanced only when the rebuild is WRITTEN — never on a refusal (so the retry survives) and never on a `ceiling` rebuild, which read no verdict and must not claim to have consumed one. **`nora_standing_rederivations_total` counts the trigger FIRING and `nora_standing_rederivations_written_total` counts it LANDING**, because on the first series alone a permanently failing fold is indistinguishable from a latched trigger — which is how the original defect read as health. **This rebuilds from the WINDOW, not from retained traces**: it breaks the drift chain, and is NOT plan task 1.7's multi-trace rebuild, which still needs `rebuild_state`'s signature changed. | Deleted with the verdict on 2026-09-24 (design/standing-compact): the trigger, watermark and verdict-read tests are gone with their subject. What replaced it is enforced by `tests/unit/test_debrief.py::test_the_prior_reaches_the_fold_on_every_turn_including_past_the_old_ceiling` and `::test_fold_count_increments_by_one_per_tag_fold_and_is_never_reset`. |

| DEC-214 | **Workspace > unit > room: a Nora WORKSPACE holds one or more units, a unit holds one or more rooms and AT MOST ONE per platform, and each Nora workspace is bound to exactly ONE Honcho workspace; inside it each unit is a Honcho NAMED SCOPE** (operator, 2026-09-28). **Retiring with Honcho (operator 2026-10-16, `design/unified-memory/35-persona.md` row 6): the unit becomes the only boundary.** Where each part lives: `policy.toml` holds the structure (`[units.<unit>] workspace = "..."`; once the table exists it must name every unit a room uses and no unit without a room, else startup is refused), `identity.toml` the external binding (`[workspaces.<name>] honcho_workspace = "..."`; unbound = the workspace's own name), and `config.toml`'s `memory.workspace_id` only the binding of the IMPLICIT workspace (`default`) every unit is in when `policy.toml` has no `[units]` — so an existing deployment and the eval harness are unchanged until the table is written. A Nora workspace and a Honcho workspace are separate names for separate things (GLOSSARY.md). `nora.app.memory_routing` resolves the three files once and refuses a binding with no `[units]`, a binding for a workspace no unit uses, two workspaces on one Honcho workspace, and a conversation id in two units. Every `MemoryStore` verb is ROUTED by the room or unit it is for (the port's `workspace_id` parameter is removed — a caller never names a Honcho workspace, the 2026-09-19 note-discharge bug), `ensure_workspace` provisions every bound Honcho workspace with Nora's peer and every unit's scope, peers are ensured and configured per (Honcho workspace, peer), each room's session is joined to its unit scope once per process — only if it is not already a member (amended 2026-09-28: honcho v3.1.2 re-enqueues a paid `scope_backfill` for every named session with messages on each add, members included, and on a session create carrying `scopes`; the member list is read first, and a failed read skips the join; `tests/unit/test_honcho_workspaces.py::test_a_second_startup_adds_nothing_and_backfills_nothing`), and `representation`, `chat` and workspace `search` pass `scope=<unit>` (the named arm). The peer card endpoint takes no `scope` in Honcho v3.1.2 and stays unscoped, bounded by the Honcho workspace; a room's session search needs none. `conclude` writes both `(nora, person)` and `(scope.<unit>, person)` in one batch, because a named-scope read swaps the observer to the scope peer and would otherwise never serve a `remember`. With `[units]`, a room or unit the policy places nowhere is refused (unavailable / False), never widened. WITHOUT `[units]` every route is UNSCOPED, exactly as before — named scopes start empty, so scoping a deployment whose config did not change would empty every recall on the day of the image change. With `[units]`, `ensure_workspace` also joins every room the policy knows (whose deterministic `nora-conv-*` session exists) to its unit scope at startup, so a quiet room's unit scope is not empty of it until it next speaks. **A bound Honcho workspace must be Nora's**: Honcho workspaces are shared by every application on the server, and the deploy host's `ridgeline` holds another application's 837 sessions (read back 2026-09-28), so a name proves nothing. Nora creates hers with workspace metadata `nora_owner = <ai_peer>`, claims one that is absent or empty, and refuses — every call, and startup — one that holds sessions without her marker; `memory.workspace_id`, which predates the marker, is exempt. DEC-105's one-room-per-platform-per-unit rule, stated and never enforced, now refuses startup in both forms of the file. The eval harness drops `[units]` and `[workspaces]` from its own copies and then asks the production router where it can reach, refusing anything outside the eval namespace. `nora memory backfill --unit <unit>` replays a unit's recorded human messages into its own Honcho workspace through the live feed path (dry run unless `--apply`, `--resume` to skip what a session holds, refuses the implicit workspace and `memory.workspace_id`'s). SUPERSEDES the operator decision of 2026-09-19 that one Nora is one Honcho workspace permanently (design/proposed/24 §S.4, `WorkspaceRouter`'s docstring) — its REASON is kept: a Honcho workspace per UNIT would split one person into N models, so units share their workspace's and only a Nora workspace splits. AMENDS DEC-66's «workspace-wide» recall to unit-wide. `nora memory carry-conclusions --workspace <w> --before <cutover>` copies Nora's session-less explicit conclusions created BEFORE the cutover (earlier `remember` and note-discharge writes, which no scope backfill copies; post-cutover `conclude` still writes such a row, so `--before` is required) into every unit scope of that workspace, in one request per row so a failure strands no scope, skipping anything any scope already holds — and only rows about a person who belongs to exactly that one workspace; rows about someone in several (or none) are listed by id for the operator, never copied. `nora memory detach-unit` takes a moved unit out of the Honcho workspace it left in two rerunnable steps: `--apply` (refused until a backfill dry run for the unit would feed nothing) records the sessions and their peers in a `--peers-file` under the ignored `state/`, then deletes the unit's `nora-conv-*` sessions (Honcho's queued session delete removes the session's messages and every document stored under it, `src/crud/session.py::delete_session`); `--refresh-cards` waits until Honcho reports no conclusion left under each deleted session, refusing rather than rebuilding early, then schedules a `card_refresh` rebuild for the recorded peers. Session-less dream conclusions are out of its reach. The backfill sends each message's own time as `created_at`, and provisions nothing until every refusal has passed. The portal's memory page shows the signed-in person one entry per Nora workspace a listed room names them in (everyone is in the one implicit workspace without `[units]`; a person only in `persons = "*"` rooms gets none with `[units]`), each read unscoped and read-only across that workspace's Honcho workspace (`workspace=` on `representation`/`peer_card`, never creating or marking a workspace). Live mapping: workspace `67` = units friends + wedding on the existing Honcho workspace `nora`; workspace `ridgeline` = unit ridgeline on Honcho workspace `nora-ridgeline`. This holds unless a scoped read is measured serving less than the unit's own rooms said, or a person's model is found blended across two Nora workspaces. **Amended 2026-09-28 by DEC-229** (`design/cognition-loop` step 0, `50-character-and-standing.md` §5): Character is per unit; the peer card, unscoped within its Honcho workspace, is never Character evidence. | The `unusual` flags are result-only (no description change) and fail-soft. **This holds unless** the `tool_selection` arm shows `routine_read` taking `where_been`'s cases or future questions still reaching `where_is`/`where_been`, in which case design/27 §4.3's measured alternative (a Level 3 `usual` arm on `where_been`) replaces it. | `tests/unit/test_routine_read.py` (`test_where_will_grant_be_on_wednesday_night`, `test_no_number_reaches_her`, `test_evidence_only_when_asked_and_as_counts_of_the_past`, `test_thin_history_is_said_inside_the_routine_as_rough`, `test_a_stranger_in_the_room_is_refused_before_any_read`, `test_a_degraded_room_is_unavailable_not_refused`), `tests/test_where_been.py::test_the_day_arm_flags_a_stay_unusual_against_their_own_past`, `tests/test_where_been.py::test_the_day_is_answered_when_the_flags_cannot_be_computed` |
| DEC-216 | **Presence serves a movement model that Nora composes, and draws the line at how people move** (design/proposed/27-presence-analytics.md §4.4, operator 2026-09-28, the «plan this dinner» scenario). Built: when someone usually arrives at or leaves a place, as habits rather than one average and, on the day itself, from the days like today (`routine_read` `what=arrival/departure`, M1); where they are now against their usual place at this hour (`routine_read` `today`, M4); the journeys they repeat with how long those actually take (`where_been` `routes` → `usual_trips`, M2); and every place a presence read names is bound for that turn to the words it was named with, which `route` takes back and resolves server side behind the same R-31 audience check, so a trip can start from «a home of theirs» with no id and no coordinate reaching the model, a reply or a link (M3; an opaque `place_ref` was built first and replaced before merge, on published tool guidance against low-level identifiers). **Not presence:** who drives (memory and the group's social context; Life360's driving flag is on for 32-87% of fixes, at rest too), travel time for a new journey (Nora composes it from `route`, maps and weather), and the planning itself (the cognition loop). | DEC-242 | **Migration step 3a-ii: the Cognition session loop in shadow, the pace verbs and self-wakes, `remind` mirrored and held, and a compare command — still no live write, no send** (`design/cognition-loop/70-migration.md` step 3a; `20-observe.md` §3; `30-cognition.md` §2; migration `0079_cognition_pace_remind` on `0078_cognition_session`). (1) `nora.app.cognition_session.CognitionSessionRunner` runs ONE session per would-wake the wake evaluator records, via the evaluator's optional `on_wake` hook, typed by ONE Protocol (`nora.domain.stimuli.WakeHook`, keyword-only `unit, view, wake_id, now_ms`) that the evaluator calls and `CognitionSessionRunner.wake_hook` returns, so mypy holds the two together (they had drifted: positional call, keyword-only receiver); `session_mode = "off"` and an empty agenda make zero model calls by control flow. **A wake's fate is ONE durable fact (second review of #627; the state machine is `nora.domain.stimuli`'s module docstring).** A wake written with the hook wired carries `tracked = 1` on its own row and awaits at most one `cognition_wake_outcome` row keyed by the WAKE (first write stands). OPEN (no outcome, younger than `[cognition] session_timeout_seconds`, 900): the unit is in flight and the wake's range is claimed (it is the watermark), whether or not a session row was ever written. CLOSED (`closed`): the watermark, and its carry rows count. FAILED (`failed`/`timeout`/`cancelled`) and EXPIRED (no outcome past the timeout: a kill, an exit before any write, an outcome write that failed): skipped by the watermark, so the wake's stimuli are pending again. Single-flight and `max_concurrent_sessions` read that (or a task alive in this process), never a wake's age; the cooldown runs from the outcome. Every exit from `on_wake` writes the outcome by wake id, so an exit before the session row (a missing home room, `build_situation` or `record_session` raising, a cancel) is `failed`/`cancelled`, not a silent watermark (this closes step 3a-ii's first-round residual); a task cancelled before its first step writes nothing and expires. **No wake swallows another's range**: `decide` refuses while the newest wake is OPEN, and `record_wake` takes a `WakeGuard` and, under a per-unit transaction-scoped advisory lock, writes only if the unit's newest wake and its outcome are still what the tick read. **A close is atomic and never late**: `StimulusStore.record_outcome` writes `closed` and its carry rows in ONE transaction under the same lock (a session is either closed with its carries or not closed); a `closed` for a wake a later wake already superseded is written `timeout` with no carries, so an expired session finishing late never closes over stimuli another session took; carries with any other outcome are refused, and the carry read also counts only rows of a `closed` wake. The session's own wall clock (`AdaptorBudget.timeout_seconds`) must end `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_SECONDS` (60) before the wake's timeout, and every unit the evaluator may wake must have a home room: both refused when the runner is built. The terminal `cancelled` write is shielded from a second cancel. A failure is RAISED after it is recorded (the evaluator counts it); `LiveCognitionAgentRunner` never swallows one into a normal return; `shutdown` cancels in-flight sessions and records them `cancelled`. **The watermark choice (20 §3, «a failed session does not advance it»): the watermark advances ONLY on a `closed` wake**; the alternative, re-appending a failed session's stimuli, was rejected because it writes duplicates into an append-only table, changes their ids and order, and loses their `waits` and due times. Because the watermark then moves past a CLOSED wake's unclosed items, those items (and the ones past `max_items`) are returned by `cognition_carry` rows with a strike (30 §2): an item left open or closed `waiting` returns `waits` (it rides the next wake, never starts one) and is `struck` at `max_strikes` (3); an item past `max_items` returns at once with a strike; a model's `close(waiting)` takes the same strike. **A strike is the ITEM's**: the strike is part of the agenda's grouping key, so a returning item stays its own item (rendered «returning: left open by N earlier sessions») and a fresh stimulus of the same room never inherits its strike. The session holds ONLY the dry-run write, pace and mirror verbs plus caller-supplied read tools; the runner takes a `CognitionDryRunStore` and narrow read callables, never a live store. (2) `wake_at`/`wake_move`/`wake_cancel` record in `cognition_self_wake` and append a `self` stimulus the evaluator already triggers on; guards: 5 LIVE pending per unit (not fired, not cancelled, not superseded, folded from the transition rows by `fold_self_wakes`), **12 `wake_at` calls per unit per rolling 24 h** (`[cognition] max_self_wakes_per_day`, a starting value: a wake that fired frees its pending slot, so a session that re-arms itself every pass is bounded by this), subject overlap supersedes, horizon from the cooldown to 7 days, own-only move/cancel across sessions (the pending seams return only cognition's rows). `wake_cancel`, `wake_move` and a superseding `wake_at` RETRACT the replaced `self` stimulus by its ref (`stimulus_retraction`); ONE retraction predicate (`nora.infra.sql.stimuli.live_stimulus`, twin `nora.testing.stimuli.live_stimulus`) is applied by every read that can surface a stimulus: the pending read, the carry side door (a carried self-wake that was then cancelled or moved never fires through carry) and the ledger's pending self-wakes. Write order so no failure loses a self-wake or fires one called off: `wake_move` appends, then retracts the rest of the ref (taking the new one back if that fails), then records; `wake_at` appends, then records (taking the stimulus back if the record fails), then retracts a superseded ref; `wake_cancel` retracts, then records. A CLOSED session records `fired` for a due self-wake on its agenda (after the close, never before). The per-day cap and the horizon read the clock at the CALL, not the session's start, and the pending self-wakes read is bounded to refs with a transition in the last 7 days plus one (`PENDING_WINDOW_SECONDS`). The pace and remind read-check-write is one critical section per unit (an `asyncio.Lock`; the process is single), so two concurrent calls cannot both pass the cap. (3) `remind`/`remind_move`/`remind_cancel` record in `cognition_remind_mirror`, never sent; `nora cognition compare --since` prints matched / cognition-only / proactive-only keyed on a note id OR an event id (bare or typed, in one room), reads each mirrored remind CHAIN at its latest state (a cancelled one is in neither count, a moved one is read at its latest time), keeps a proactive row with no key as `unkeyed` instead of dropping it, and prints a notes section (cancelled, moved, unkeyed, unkeyable) for whatever the three counts leave out by construction. (4) #625 review follow-ups: `dry_run_note_create` refuses a duplicate open title and `dry_run_event_propose` refuses two open proposed events through the extracted live functions (`has_duplicate_open_title`, `still_open_gatherings`); | DEC-249 | **The data model: five layers in one flow, Memory beside them, one entry in the Notebook, and the hierarchy Layer › Tier › Kind › Entry** (operator, agreed and corrected 2026-10-01: "we need clean topologies and hierarchies before we really start building"; "I prefer meaningful and accurate names"; `design/cognition-loop/05-data-model.md` is canonical for the topology and the vocabulary, `10-tiers.md` for the Notebook's tiers and the two layers they cite). (1) **Layers, each defined by who writes it and how it is derived, in flow order**: **Authored** (doctrine, config, policy, identity; humans only; versioned files) → **Record** (raw observations: transcripts, audio, photos and their perceptions, reactions, edits, presence, face labels, Nora's own sends, acts, tool calls and their results, and artifacts; written by code at the moment it happens: ingestion for what others do, the turn and fire paths for her own acts, the recording verbs for a person's statement; append-only, hidden on forget) → **Rollup** (computed from the Record by code; deterministic, rebuildable) → **Notebook** (Nora's judgement: entries citing the Record and Rollup; the subconscious, one writer per tier: Cognition, fast and per group, for the Register and Standing; the Character adaptor and the Lessons adaptor, slow reflection, for Character and Lessons; Assess writes nothing, it reports; revised, withdrawn, versioned) → **Views** (per-reader slices assembled at read time through ONE assembly path under lineage and withdrawal; never stored as data, though a View may be recorded as provenance; the operator reads operator-only rows through an operator View). **Memory** (Honcho: per-person understanding and what people say about themselves) sits beside the flow, outside our system; it may be read into Views and is never copied into the Notebook. The operator: "the data model here is the data warehouse, and the raw audio or the transcript is the data lake"; who said what is "the responsibility of the memory system". The analogy's words (lake, warehouse, mart) and medallion names are not used as names. (2) **Boundary rules**: one-way flow Record → Rollup → Notebook → Views, nothing writes backwards (her speech enters the Record as an observation); only the Record and the Rollup computed from it are evidence; one writer per layer and, in the Notebook, per tier; speaking turns only read Views and speak, and to change the Notebook raise a stimulus (a «記低» about the unit or the end of a tag turn is a strong cue, about two minutes); scope (person, room, unit, workspace) explicit on every row, the unit the read boundary (DEC-231). (3) **Vocabulary**: a **tier** is a subdivision inside the Notebook only (Register, Character, Standing, Lessons); a **kind** is a row type within a tier (note, memo, event; person, room, unit, Nora; room, unit, person; lesson); an **entry** is one row. The Record and the Rollup are layers, not tiers: this narrows "tier" as DEC-217 used it. (4) **The entry**: one object with one machinery (storage, revisions, citations, the withdrawal cascade, lineage, as-of reads, read verbs, Views), storing its reasoning mode and confidence (a View shows the mode as `observed` or `inferred`), with no statement-level provenance; an abduced value always goes out as a question, whatever its confidence, and is never upgraded by assent; what differs per kind is a rule with its own test, because unifying hides differences and does not remove them. No knowledge graph: typed relational references (citations into the Record and Rollup, about-references, links between entries), and a link is never evidence (amends `10-tiers.md` §2 rule 1). (5) **One writer per tier, and the conscious never writes the Notebook** (operator: "the subconscious, one writer per tier"): the tag path's note and event writes and the debrief's Standing write move behind Cognition at step 4 (amends `10-tiers.md` §2 rule 3), handed off by a `handoff` stimulus raised by code when a tag turn ends (the one Nora-originated stimulus, amending `20-observe.md` §3), which requires her tool calls and results in the Record first; `remind` and `cancel_reminder` stay on the tag turn as machinery, and Cognition may cancel a person's reminder with the event it cancels on `told` evidence. The operator may retire or correct an entry, never author one (`source='operator'`). Machinery (stimuli, wakes, sessions, reminders) is append-only state with named writers, not a layer. "Layer" is reserved for the data layers; the operator's mind model is named the conscious and the subconscious (明意識 / 潛意識), never "layers". (6) **Migration**: E1a (the `citation` table widened to events and Rollup keys with a `part` column; events in the cascade; event lineage written) gates step 4; E1b, memo as the first kind built on the entry, right after step 3's shadow week (was step 7), gated on its corpus; E1c, her tool calls in the Record, before E2; unit-wide kinds whose text places nobody take lineage from `about`; a note's `## From memory` retires at convergence and the curator's discharge into Honcho dies with the curator; Character of a person, the unit and Nora, Lessons, and unit and person Standing are born on it at step 8; the existing kinds converge as each is touched, under render parity, no table dropped; the live Standing path (DEC-239) and live notes are not disrupted before their kinds converge. Open, not ruled, each with the author's and an independent review's recommendation (`05-data-model.md` §10): when culture moves onto the entry; how the six stored reasoning modes relate to the two shown; the portal's events page through Views. **This holds unless** a converged kind is measured losing a row, a citation or a withdrawal its separate store kept, or the hand-off is measured dropping a write the tag path used to make. | NOT ENFORCED — design only; each kind's rules get their tests when that kind is built on the entry (`design/cognition-loop/05-data-model.md` §3, §9) |
| DEC-250 | **A Cognition session's verbs are held to what the session did and saw: a `written` close needs a write, `remind` is bound to a room, a note write runs the tag path's validator on what was shown and fetched, every verb takes one time base, and a Standing revise is checked against the revision id** (`design/cognition-loop/30-cognition.md` §2-§3; review of 2026-09-30, B3, B4, M3, M5, M6, m4; built 2026-10-01; operator: "yes to all", 2026-09-30). (1) **B3, closing.** `close(reason="written")` is refused `no_write_for_item` unless this session recorded a `would_commit` write FOR that item (note, event or Standing; a refused write, a `remind` and a `wake_at` are not writes): the write verbs take an optional `item` (the agenda index), and a write that names none backs only the sole item of its room (amended on the #663 review: it was any write in the item's room). It was the model's say-so. The other reasons need no write. (2) **B4, act.** (`remind_move` and `remind_cancel` refuse `unknown_room` for a pending reminder whose room is off today's agenda.) `remind(intent, subject_rows, at, room)` takes `room` like every other write verb and resolves it through the agenda (`unknown_room`, `room_required`); it took a free `room_platform` and `room_conversation_id`, so it could reach a room the agenda never named. The design's `remind(at, room, brief)` has no `why`, so none is added. (3) **M3, notes.** The note dry run builds `Shown` from the session's own evidence: the grounding records of THAT room (id, author, person id, whether they are Nora's; a deleted message whose words were withheld is not citable), the records `record_query` returned, the room's roster (read through `Room.members`; an unreadable roster is `unavailable`, never every owner refused) and Nora's names, so the SAME `parse_note_body` runs as on the tag path: an `## Owed` owner on the roster passes, a stranger is refused `unknown_owner`, a line attributed to Nora is refused, and a name is checked against the author of the message the line cites. The blanket `unknown_owner` and the pass-through for an attribution nothing could verify are gone. (4) **m4, fetched.** A note may cite ids the session FETCHED, not only those it was shown (30 §3 check 1): `note_read`'s cited ids are carried, `record_query`'s rows are checked against their sender, and a Rollup row `rollup_read` returned is cited as `rollup(kind|subject|from/to)` inside a line's trailing brackets (`nora.domain.note_body.rollup_key`, new rule `unknown_rollup_key`; a Rollup row says who was where, so an attributed line may not rest on one alone). The session watches those three reads' own results (`nora.agent.fetch_watch`); what lineage withheld was never fetched. What a read returned is kept PER ROOM, under the room it was routed through (the call's `room` argument, or the one room of the agenda), and a note written to a room is shown only that room's fetched rows (a row read through room A is not citable in room B; #663 review). `record_query` prints each row's message `n` for the Cognition session only, never on a tag turn (R-18). (5) **M5, one time base.** `wake_at`, `wake_move`, `remind` and `remind_move` take `at` and an event takes `when`, each ISO 8601 WITH an offset, and a note's `anchor_date` is an ISO date, converted in code; a naive, empty or unparseable time is refused `bad_time` (`bad_when`, `bad_anchor_date`). They were epoch milliseconds, ISO and `YYYYMMDD`. (6) **M6, the token.** `standing_revise`'s `base_revision_id` is the `standing_revision.id` `standing_read` shows as `revision` (amends DEC-239 (4)): `fold_count` did not move when the ingest fold rewrote the head, so a stale base passed. A base against a head with no revision id is stale. **Not covered:** the Register citation edges for events (M2), open events across `proposed` and `confirmed` (M4), and the live `standing_revise` being called by any caller with a base (neither fold asserts one). **This holds unless** a shadow-week reading shows `no_write_for_item` refusing a close a written item deserved because the model did not name the item on a write in a room with several. | , `::test_a_tag_turns_record_query_prints_no_ids`; `tests/unit/test_note_body.py::test_a_rollup_row_the_write_did_not_read_is_refused`, `::test_a_rollup_row_does_not_say_who_said_a_line`; `tests/unit/test_standing_revise.py::test_a_base_behind_the_current_revision_is_stale`; `tests/unit/test_cognition_session_tool_specs.py::test_every_verb_has_named_typed_parameters_and_no_kwargs`; `tests/unit/test_tool_catalogue.py::test_a_tag_catalogue_holds_no_dreamer_only_line`; mutation table `scripts/mutations/cognition-c.json` |
| DEC-253 | **DEPRECATED 2026-10-03 (DEC-277): the code this decided was deleted at the Cognition cut-over; the row stays for its history.** **An event's write carries its evidence: cited ids, a reasoning and a confidence held to what the session saw, an abduced value kept as a question, every status before `happened` reachable, a `citation` edge and a per-field lineage written with the event, and the withdrawal cascade and every event reader honouring it** (`design/cognition-loop/40-register.md` §3-§4, `12-schemas.md` §3, `10-tiers.md` §2 rule 7 and §3, `70-migration.md` §5 "Events."; review of 2026-09-30 M2, M4, m6 and of #662 M8 (E1a), m4, m6; migration `0086_event_citations`; built 2026-10-01). (1) **The verbs.** `event_propose`, `event_revise` and `event_set_status` take `reasoning` (`told`, `deduced`, `abduced`: the three 40 §4 and 10 §4 allow an event, not the six modes of the other tiers, so `induced`, `computed` and `said` are refused `bad_reasoning`), `confidence` (`low`, `medium`, `high`) and `cited_ids` (message ids as digits, Rollup rows as `rollup(kind|subject|from/to)`), all required. Citations are held to `Shown` by the function a note's brackets use (`nora.domain.note_body.check_citations` over `_check_ids`): a message the session was shown or fetched (`record_query`, `note_read`), in THAT room, not one of Nora's own, a Rollup row it read; refused `unknown_id`, `cites_nora`, `unknown_rollup_key`, `uncited`. Every write needs one, except a move to `lapsed`, whose evidence is the date passing and no row. One write has one reasoning, so a time and a place resting on different evidence are two writes. `event_propose` takes `status` `staged` or `proposed` (30 §2) and refuses anything later `bad_status`; a move out of a status after `happened` is refused `terminal_status`. (2) **Abduced is stored and voiced as a question.** An abduced value is STORED like any other, with its mode (`FieldMeta.reasoning = abduced` on the field it states), and every reader voices it as a question, never as a stated fact (`nora.domain.gatherings.render_field`, one place a reader asks; 40 §4: "a value that rests only on abduction goes out as a question", 10 §2 rule 4 and the §5 dinner case: place → C on the route request alone "would be abduced, and anything she said about it would go out as a question"). A person's "yeah" to her own guess is no write, and a write that states other fields leaves the field's mode alone (`merge_field_meta`), so only a write that restates the field on evidence of its own can change how it was reached. The first cut of this step made an abduced write create nothing; that contradicted 40 §4 and is reversed. (3) **M4.** `_open_events` (was `_proposed_events`) reads every status before `happened` (`OPEN_STATUSES`: staged, proposed, confirmed), so a confirmed event reaches `happened` or `cancelled`; the session and the cognition grounding both read it, and the `event_propose` ambiguity backstop still counts `proposed` events only, since a staged event is a guess and a confirmed one is settled. (4) **The edges.** Migration `0086` widens `citation.citing_store` to `event` and `cited_store` to `rollup` (the key text), adds `citation.part` (nullable; `NULL` on every row written before, the field name on an event's), and makes the edge unique over `part` with `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (two whole-row edges still collapse; one message cited for two fields is two edges). `GatheringStore.create` and `update` take an `EventEvidence` (the parts the write states, the `EventCitation`s, the room a turn was said in) and, in the write's own transaction, leave one edge per citation and compute the lineage (`nora.infra.sql.event_evidence`). `events.field_meta` and `event_revision.field_meta` hold each field's own `reasoning`, `confidence` and `as_of` (10 §3 gives an event those per field, and 0074 could carry them row-level only). (5) **m6: lineage has a writer.** `event_lineage` computes each stated field's lineage from its own citations: `message:<room it was said in>` per cited message, the entries a cited Rollup row's own lineage holds (`rollup_lineage` finds the current-build row by its key, to the second, in the event's unit), `unresolved` at the origin for a message gone or hidden, a Rollup key that matches no current row or names another unit's, and a field with nothing behind it. A restated field is REPLACED, not unioned, since the value it states rests on the evidence it cites; fields a write leaves alone keep theirs. **Its EDGES are replaced the same way** (`record_event_citations`: every edge the event holds for a part the write restates is deleted and the write's own inserted, a part restated with no citation keeps none), so the cascade follows what the event rests on NOW: create cites A for the time, a revision restates it on B, withdrawing A marks nothing. The `citation` table therefore moved from APPEND_ONLY to a HISTORY table (migration `0086`, `nora_row_history`): a replaced edge is kept as a `delete` version, so what an earlier revision rested on stays re-derivable. The mark stays row-level (`events.unsupported_at`, 05 §3 "withdrawal"), not per field: 05 and 10 give `part` to lineage and the edges, and the event row is what is withdrawn. `as_of` is the newest cited message's time. **The tag path cites the message that raised the turn**: `Room.trigger_message_ids` (the tagger's Record row at the message's own time, `nora.agent.room.trigger_message_ids`, code's own knowledge, no tool text changed) rides `create_event`/`update_event`/`set_event_status` into `_tag_evidence`, one edge per stated field, so forgetting that message's author marks the event; its lineage is `message:<room>` per field exactly as before (the same value with and without the edge), so `[lineage] mode` reads no difference. (6) **The cascade and its readers.** `events.unsupported_at`; `withdraw_messages` marks an event whose edge reaches the withdrawn message (`nora.app.withdrawal._mark_event`, idempotent, never overwriting the first mark), `nora person forget` reaches it through the same call, `clear_unsupported` lifts it by the same predicate as the other three heads, and `_event_values` never writes the mark, so an update built from a row read before the cascade cannot put it back. Readers: `SqlGatheringStore.search` (`event_search`) and `list_for_conversation` and `list_for_person` (the portal) leave it out (`include_unsupported` exists for a caller that re-writes every row); `GatheringStore.get` returns the real row, for a writer; `GatheringService.get_event`, `get_event_for_person` (the portal's page, 404) and `_require_in_conversation` (the tag path's revise, status, RSVP and venue) read it as an unknown id; the cognition grounding drops it in every lineage mode; and the heartbeat's new `GatheringScreen` (`nora.app.gathering_screen`, a second fire-time screen beside `ProactiveScreen`) HOLDS the reminder a withdrawn event owns, because a gathering's reminder carries the event's title in its payload and the fire turn composes from that alone, never reading the event. **Held, not cancelled** (10 §2 rule 7: withdrawal stops rendering and is reversible by `unforget`/`clear_unsupported`): the row stays `PENDING`, is not fired and not resolved, and is counted on `nora_gathering_reminders_held_total{reason=unsupported}` per row per tick. The hold is DERIVED from the event's mark (one copy of the fact; `_mark_event` writes nothing to the reminder and `clear_unsupported` has nothing else to undo), and lasts until `due_at + HOLD_GRACE` (2 h): a mark cleared inside it lets the reminder fire late on the next tick, a mark still in place at that point resolves it `CANCELLED` / `expired_while_held` (a distinct outcome on `nora_reminders_fired_total`, whose help now names every outcome a screen can write), and a mark cleared after does not revive it. An event that cannot be READ is held too (`reason=read_error`), never terminal: a transient database error must not cost a legitimate reminder its life, the next tick reads again. `list_reminders` leaves a held reminder out (`GatheringService.held_reminder_ids`; unavailable, never the full list, when that cannot be read). A revision does not clear the mark (a note's does not either): a writer's next session re-derives. **Changes on merge (live):** a tag turn's event writes now carry `message:<room>` lineage per field (no effect while `[lineage] mode = "off"`); `event_search`, the portal and the tag path's event tools stop seeing an event a withdrawal marked; a due gathering reminder whose event was marked is held (fired late if the mark clears inside two hours of its time, else expired_while_held) and is not listed; an event write on a tag turn cites the message that raised it, and a note's Rollup citation records an edge and takes the Rollup row's lineage (`rollup_keys_in`; `cited_ids_in` now also reads the ids of a group that mixes ids and keys, which it missed); the migration also attaches `nora_row_history` to `citation`; the migration adds columns to `events` and `event_revision` and rewrites the `citation` constraints (no row is rewritten). The Cognition verbs stay in dry run, so nothing they validate commits. **Not built (recorded, not hidden):** the `<events>` block does not exist on the tag path (70 §8 lists it as a new block), so per-field reasoning rendering, "place: C, told 18:40", is left to the step that adds it; the mode cap (30 §3 check 5: a value resting on presence fixes older than 900 s is capped at `abduced`) needs fix ages no verb is handed; `exclude_persons` is not unioned from citations (check 7); the `Plan`, `Open`, `Happened` and `Changes` body (12 §3) is not composed, so the per-field mode lives in `field_meta` and the edges' `part`; a withdrawn Rollup row does not cascade, since `withdraw_messages` walks message edges and the rollups recompute on the next pass. **This holds unless** a shadow week shows `uncited` refusing a write the session rightly made on evidence it could not cite (a lapse is exempt, a revision after a silence is not), or a tag turn whose triggering row is not in its window (`trigger_message_ids` empty: the event then records the room and no edge, and the cascade cannot reach it) turns out to be common. | `tests/unit/test_cognition_session_events_d.py` (M2: `::test_a_proposal_citing_a_message_the_session_was_shown_would_commit_with_its_evidence`, `::test_a_proposal_citing_a_message_it_was_never_shown_is_refused_unknown_id`, `::test_a_proposal_with_no_citation_or_one_of_nora_s_own_messages_is_refused`, `::test_a_rollup_row_is_citable_only_once_the_session_read_it`, `::test_a_message_the_session_fetched_with_record_query_is_citable`, `::test_a_mode_the_event_tier_does_not_allow_is_refused`, `::test_an_abduced_proposal_is_stored_with_its_mode_and_voiced_as_a_question`, `::test_an_abduced_revision_changes_the_field_and_keeps_the_others_modes`; | DEC-251 | **`media_search` also finds photos PEOPLE SENT, in the calling room only: a `scope` argument (`library` by default, `room`) and a `days` look-back of 1 to 90 on the one existing tool. DEC-138 is AMENDED IN PART: its «never inbound» custody scope stays the default and is no longer the only scope** (operator decision 2026-10-01; `design/artifact/00-design.md` §25; `nora.agent.tools.media_search`, `nora.domain.media.room_sightings`, `RecordStore.media_rows`, `MediaObjectStore.lookup_search`). (1) **The room is the message row, never the media index.** A photo is returned only when a message of THIS conversation (the turn's own `conversation_id`, never a model argument) carries its sha256; the index row is joined only for the text (`title`, `description`, `content`), and its `provenance` is never the gate and is not searched, because it names only the FIRST room a byte string was seen in. So a photo first indexed in room A is never found from room B unless room B's own messages carry it, and a photo re-sent into room B is found in room B. (2) **One tool, not two.** Fixed options are a `Literal` in the signature (ADR 0015 §4), the name is unchanged (ADR 0004), and the sibling set stays `media_fetch` (in view) / `media_search` (find) / `media_send` (deliver her own); `media_send` still delivers only `generated` and `fetched` media. (3) **Recency is a filter** because people refer to photos by time: `days` is clamped to 90, the `room` scope defaults to 90 and `library` to no bound; results are the newest 10, each with its 6-hex marker code, kind, when it was sent (RFC 3339) and its stored description, which passes the same identifier screen as every serve of media. No sender, person, room id or platform is ever returned. Stickers are not separable from photos in `media_json` and stay in; shared-item covers, voice notes, documents and her own sent rows are out. (4) **`unavailable` is not «nothing».** `search` swallowed a database error as `()`; `lookup_search` (beside `lookup` and `lookup_prefix`) reports `available=False`, and a message-store or index error in either scope is `unavailable` with a note. A photo nothing has read yet cannot match words and is COUNTED in the note, not silently dropped. (5) **A code room search returned is usable by its code.** `nora.domain.media.room_sightings` (with `code_matches`, `ROOM_MEDIA_DAYS = 90`, `ROOM_MEDIA_ROWS = 1000`) is the ONE resolver for `media_fetch`, `computer_import` and room search: the room's recent window plus its last 90 days of human media rows, by the message row, newest first, the room never a model argument; a 6-hex handle matching two blobs is `ambiguous`, never picked. The row cap is 1000 (the busiest real room holds about 410 in 90 days) and is over-fetched by one: a read that hit it is `truncated`, room search says older media was not searched, and a code not found in a truncated read is `unavailable`, never `nothing_found`. A reading is screened whole (title, description, content) by the same identifier screen `media_fetch` uses, and a screened reading is neither returned nor matched on. Videos are included (their reading is the index row's `content`; `video_readings` is a composite-keyed cache of deliberate reads and is not searched). **Not covered:** stickers cannot be told from photos in `media_json` and stay in; voice notes are `audio/*` entries and are left out of room search (they still resolve by code); `generate_image`'s reference resolver keeps its own window; the `tool_selection` routing cases for this change are written, not run. **This holds unless** a room may see another room's photos, which would be a new decision, not a reading of this one. | `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_photo_sent_in_room_a_is_never_found_from_room_b`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_photo_re_sent_into_room_b_is_found_in_room_b`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_days_excludes_a_photo_sent_before_the_window`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_an_unreadable_message_store_is_unavailable_never_no_photos`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_the_library_scope_reports_an_unreadable_index_as_unavailable`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_her_own_generated_media_is_still_found_by_default`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_code_found_by_room_search_30_days_back_resolves_in_media_fetch`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_media_beyond_90_days_is_not_found`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_room_video_is_found_by_a_word_from_its_reading`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_title_holding_an_identifier_is_withheld_with_the_rest`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_withheld_reading_cannot_be_probed_one_query_at_a_time`, `tests/unit/test_media_search_room.py::test_a_code_behind_the_row_cap_is_unavailable_never_nothing_found`, `tests/contract/test_audit_store_contract.py::test_media_rows_reach_past_the_recent_window_newest_first`, `tests/contract/test_media_object_store_contract.py::test_lookup_search_is_search_with_the_availability_axis` |
| DEC-252 | **DEPRECATED 2026-10-03 (DEC-277): the code this decided was deleted at the Cognition cut-over; the row stays for its history.** **AMENDED 2026-10-02 (PR #712, an audit of the live shadow data): (3)'s "deliberately closed" is no longer evidence, and `closed` no longer counts the model's own word.** A close is the MODEL's statement, and the model is what is measured (AGENTS.md: no self-attestation). So a close that meets (3)'s conditions is reported as `closed self-attested: not evidence`, never as closed; a clocked-only row is `closed by code` only when the row carries a note or event id, the close is `covered`, and the close's OWN session recorded a `would_commit` write of the same tier in the same room for THAT id (a creation names no existing id and proves no row; another tier or another id proves nothing); a row with no id (a Standing row, a keyless proactive row) is NEVER closed by code. `open` is every clocked-only row not closed by code, the self-attested ones included, and the three numbers print in one order: closed by code, closed self-attested (not evidence), open. A window in which no session ran is an ERROR with no tiers (never a table of zeros), every report carries a coverage line (sessions, units, per day in the `[cognition]` zone, wakes that never became a session, sessions with no skill injected) and says what `matched` does and does not establish, and the JSON report is `schema` 2: its `closed` key is gone (it meant the self-attested count too) and `closed_by_code`, `closed_self_attested` replace it. Everything below is as decided 2026-10-01 except that reading of (3).** **Migration step 3a gate: `nora cognition compare` measures the Cognition session against EVERY live clocked writer, per tier and per writer, and never decides the gate** (review B1 and D5, 2026-09-30; `design/cognition-loop/70-migration.md` step 3a and step 4; `nora.domain.cognition_shadow_compare`, `nora.app.cognition_compare`). The command compared only `cognition_remind_mirror` against `reminders kind='proactive'`, so the step-3 gate ("over a shadow week every clocked-adaptor write is matched or deliberately closed") had no instrument for notes, events, Standing or culture. (1) Per clocked writer, three counts and one line: matched, cognition-only (tier-wide, since a would-write is not attributable to one writer), clocked-only split into closed by code, closed self-attested (not evidence) and open (= every row not closed by code, the self-attested included; see the amendment above); writers are `note-candidates`, `note-curation`, `note-merge` (from `note_revision.established_by`), `event:<written_by>` (none today: `written_by = 'tag'` is the live tag path, step 4 does not retire it, and it is reported in its own "tag path (not retired)" section, in no per-writer verdict), `standing-debrief` and `standing-ingest-fold` (derived: the debrief fold increments `fold_count`, the ingest fold carries it), `culture`, `proactive` (`reminders`) and `proactive-decide` (`decision_log`). (2) Matching is one-to-one, greedy and deterministic inside a time tolerance. The default is 65 minutes, DERIVED, not chosen: the cadence of the hourly clocked writers (`note-candidates`, and `note-merge` in shadow) plus one scheduler tick (`[dreamer.schedule] tick_seconds = 300`); a clocked write is stamped when the hourly pass ran and the cognition would-write when the wake fired, so the two can differ by up to a cadence. The daily writers (`note-curation` at the 00:00 floor, the Standing folds at `fold_interval_seconds = 86400`) run once a day, so the default shows their rows clocked-only more often; `--tolerance-minutes 1445` reads them, as a widening and not a pass, and a narrow tolerance errs toward open. A note update matches by note id; a note create by room and anchor read AS OF the revision (from `row_history`, not the note row a later curation moved) AND the same title (normalised) or a shared non-empty entity set; an event by event id or by room and title. Standing matches by room and time only, and the write does not record which messages the fold read, so "the would-write came after the clocked write's input window" cannot be checked: a Standing pair is reported COINCIDENT, never matched. The act tiers by room plus note or event id inside the window with no time tolerance. (3) A clocked-only row is EXPLAINED (not closed, since the 2026-10-02 amendment above: an explaining close is `closed by code` only when it meets the amendment's proof, and is otherwise `closed self-attested`, which is not evidence and stays open) by a `cognition_session_close` with reason `no_change`, `waiting` or `covered` only when: its agenda item is in the row's room; the item's kind maps to the row's tier (`message` to note, event, Standing and the act tiers; `time` to note, event and the act tiers; `rollup` to Standing; `self`, `social`, `play` and culture to none); where the row has a note or event id the item names it (a close naming no id explains only id-less rows); the close is AFTER the clocked write and within the tolerance; and it is the nearest unused such close, so one close explains ONE row, not every row in its room. A refused would-write nearby closes nothing. `written` (self-attested, B3) and `struck` (code's strike) explain nothing. The first build let one `waiting` close explain every clocked-only row in a room and window, across writers; review 2026-10-01. (4) Fail-closed: a source that cannot be read makes its tier ERROR with no counts, never zero, and the exit code is 1; culture has no cognition verb and is reported clocked-only by construction. (5) Read-only; output carries ids, room labels and times, never message text, titles, anchors, member names or a conversation id: a room is its policy label or `room#<hash>`, and a Standing row is keyed by its room, so it carries no key (the first build printed the bare id, a phone-shaped group id, as `key`; review 2026-10-01). This holds unless a shadow week shows the tolerance or the closing rule mislabels a clocked-only row (an unrelated no_change closing a real omission), in which case the rule is tightened, not the gate loosened. | `tests/infra/test_cognition_shadow_compare_read.py::test_a_note_update_matches_the_revision_of_the_same_note_by_its_writer`;
