| DEC-254 | (AMENDED IN PART 2026-10-08, ADR 0023: the "Kept too" Drop paths below, its artifact READ path, link shortener and `/api/artifacts`, are deleted with the whole service.) **Smith, `make_artifact`, `LocalDockerBackend`, the host `docker.sock` mount, the `nora-compute` network with its `compute-egress` proxy, and Drop's `POST /api/tokens` are retired (S3b; operator decision 4, 2026-09-30; amends DEC-99 part (3) with DEC-100, DEC-101 and DEC-104, `design/sandbox-runtime/00-design.md` §6, §13; DEC-243).** Both preconditions the design set were met live on 2026-10-01: the first `computer_export` (a CSV to chat) and the first `document_publish` (ADR 0020), so a FILE now leaves through the computer and a DOCUMENT through the document tool, and the old path has no job left. What went: `nora/compute/smith/` and its image, `nora/infra/compute/docker_backend.py` with its egress allowlist, `_check_compute_egress` and the compute secret checks in composition, the `make_artifact` tool (its `NATIVE_TOOLS` row, budget and spec; the name joins `_RENAMED_SINCE`), the R-45 context nudge that existed only for it (DEC-101 DEPRECATED), the `[compute]` keys that configured the backend (`sandbox_image`, `job_timeout_seconds`, `max_concurrent_jobs`, `mem_limit`, `nano_cpus`, `data_host_root_env`), the `docker` Python dependency, the `group_add` of the host docker GID, and in Drop the token mint and the scoped job tokens (`DROP_JOB_TOKEN_SECRET`, `pyjwt`). The nora container therefore holds no control over the host Docker daemon, which closes the privilege the socket mount named and the model key that Smith was handed. **Kept, on purpose (decision 4):** the `ComputeJob` outbox, `ComputeJobPoller`, boot recovery, the `ComputeBackend` port and the `compute_jobs` table, as the generic deferred-delivery path a future `delegate_task` will use. | DEC-263 | **The VM's /workspace is backed up nightly to the host, verified, and `destroy` refuses to run without a backup** (operator 2026-10-01: the audit saw three recreates in 24 hours; `design/sandbox-runtime/00-design.md` §7; `deploy/computer/nora-computer` `backup`, `restore`, `destroy`; `nora-computer-backup.timer`; `deploy/computer/README.md`). A recreate or destroy deletes the whole VM disk, the only copy of every room's files. `nora-computer backup` tars `/workspace` inside the VM as root, copies it out, and keeps it only if the digest computed in the VM equals the copy's and the copy reads back as a gzip tar; an archive that does not verify is deleted and the run fails without touching an older one. Inside the VM the archive is made under umask 077 in a `mktemp -d` directory (root's, 0700), never in the shared `/tmp`, and the directory is removed and checked gone (a leftover fails the backup). A VM with no rooms is not backed up, so an empty `/workspace` after a recreate cannot push out the last backup that holds rooms; the backup `destroy` takes is filed under `destroy/`, outside the rotation. Each room's `browser/` (a credential store, never backed up, design §7) and computerd's `.tmux` sockets are left out by literal paths, so a project folder called `browser` is kept. A stopped VM is skipped, not started. `restore` needs the checksum, reads the archive on the host and refuses it whole if any member could write outside a room (an absolute or `..` name, a top level that is not a room, a device node or fifo, a link that leaves its room, a write through a link: `archive_check.py`), refuses over existing rooms without `--force`, copies into a private `mktemp -d` directory in the VM, checks the digest again inside the VM before extracting, and gives each room's directory to `c-<first 12 hex>` created the way computerd creates it (`chown -hR`). `destroy` takes a backup first (starting a stopped VM for it) and refuses with exit 9, removing nothing, unless `--no-backup`, which the audit row records. It is rollback on the same host, not off-host backup, and it replaces the design's never-built per-room `projects/` tar into the blob store as the answer to the loss that happened. | DEC-276 | **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-03 (guard removal; AGENTS.md «A guard needs a consequence»: 2 deletes in 5,984 messages, 0 held deletes, Honcho keeps the text anyway).** The cascade, `nora person forget`/`unforget`, held deletes (`orphan_delete`, dropped by 0092) with their matching, caps, sweep, metrics and alerts are deleted. What stays: a platform delete hides the message (`RecordStore.hide_message`). The `citation` table and the `unsupported_at` columns, which nothing read or marked any more, are dropped by migration 0093. Original text follows. **A message its platform deletes or unsends is hidden and what is derived from it as EVIDENCE is withdrawn: notes, events and staged note proposals, not the Standing and culture heads** (PR #711; operator's bar «block cross-group disclosure and honour forgetting»; the orchestrator's decisions of 2026-10-02 on the review of #711; `design/cognition-loop/10-tiers.md` §2 rule 7; `70-migration.md` §2 row 2c; extends DEC-238, amends DEC-245 (3); `nora.app.delete_withdrawal`, `nora.app.withdrawal.EVIDENCE_STORES`, `nora.ingest.stages.touch`). **Found:** all four parsers emitted a delete and the touch stage recorded it as a `message_delete` row and nothing else (`withdraw_message` had no caller; measured live: two deletes on record, both targets visible), so an unsent message kept rendering in every transcript and in everything citing it. **(1) One transaction:** `SqlDeleteWithdrawer.withdraw` sets `messages.hidden_at` and runs the cascade; a cascade that raises rolls the hide back (`cascade_failed`). The `message_delete` record is committed FIRST so a failed withdrawal is always findable; it is retried three times and `reconcile_deletes --apply` runs at every start and as `nora withdrawal reconcile-deletes`. Idempotent: `already_hidden` keeps the first hide time and the cascade runs again, a row written after the hide is marked at write time (`citation.mark_if_cites_hidden`). The write-time check reads the cited messages FOR SHARE, so a hide waits for a writer and one of the two marks the row, and the sweep re-scans the edges of messages a delete already hid. **A delete whose target is not on record** (overtook its message, arrived after a restart, or its lookup failed) is kept in `orphan_delete` (migration `0088_orphan_delete`), written first, applied directly to the row when the message is audited and by the start-up sweep (one shared key-and-authorship rule), bounded by a unique key, a 3-day TTL, an AGE WINDOW and soft caps enforced by EVICTION (never by refusing a new one). **Age window: an ASSUMPTION about the ingest paths, not a proof (rounds 6 and 7).** A delete whose target is not on record AND is older than 30 minutes when the delete arrives (`ORPHAN_RACE_WINDOW_MS`, edge exactly 30:00 held, 30:00.001 stale) is DROPPED, not held, and counted `orphan_stale_target`. What the window measures is how long the sender waited before deleting; what a held delete is FOR is a different interval, whether the delete reaches Nora BEFORE its message. The assumption is that a message reaches Nora within seconds of being sent (a photo's custody fetch, a task scheduled late), that a restart replays nothing, that Signal is strictly serial, and that no history backfill exists, so a target older than 30 minutes is a message from before she joined, one she never records (her own sends, embed-only posts), or pruned. Two paths are known to break it and neither is verified: a Discord gateway RESUME replaying an outage longer than the window (how long Discord keeps a session resumable is NOT confirmed) and a linked Signal device with a skewed clock. There the delete is dropped, the message is then recorded and **stays visible and is fed to memory: the leak direction.** Probes P1 and P1b reproduced exactly that. `nora withdrawal reconcile-deletes` does NOT recover it (a dropped delete leaves no record and no held row); the sender deleting the message again does (it is on record now), as does `nora person forget` for a whole person. WhatsApp and Instagram handles carry no time, so those deletes are always held, and a lookup that FAILED is never taken for «not there» (it is held). **Caps:** 40 per named deleter (counted across the platform), 500 unnamed per room (Discord and Instagram name nobody, so every row has an empty deleter), 1000 per room, 10000 overall. **Eviction order:** per deleter (its own oldest: true of this scope only), then per room (the oldest row of the deleter holding the MOST rows there; a deleter whose rows are all claimed by other writers is passed over for the NEXT-heaviest, never for the room's oldest row), then overall (oldest). **Arithmetic, not mechanism, is what protects a small room:** the per-deleter cap of 40 holds across the platform, so five colluding WhatsApp members hold at most 200 rows and never reach the room cap of 1000; the room scope is reached only by more than 25 flooding members, and then heaviest-first spares a victim's lone row unless every deleter holds a single one. On Discord and Instagram the unnamed cap of 500 always binds BEFORE the room scope, so heaviest-first only matters for WhatsApp and Signal rooms. Rows are claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so two writers never wait on each other's rows (the reviewer measured about 525 deadlocks with the plain delete), and the touch stage makes four attempts (three retries) with random pauses before counting `orphan_lost`. **A new held delete lands unless a concurrent writer deadlocks and all four attempts fail (`orphan_lost`), and any held delete can be evicted by a flood at the room or overall scope or, on Discord and Instagram, by 500 unnamed deletes of recent-looking ids in that room while its message is on the way.** Eviction, a lost write, a stale-target skip and the TTL are each a LEAK-direction loss if the delete's message then arrives (it stays visible and is fed to memory; Honcho cannot forget). **They were not loud:** a loss was a counter and one log line with no ids, and Prometheus loses a rare series across restarts, so round 7 adds `OrphanDeleteLost` (any `orphan_lost` in 1h) and `OrphanDeleteEvicted` (more than 50 `orphan_evicted` in 1h; 50 is a pick, unmeasured) in `deploy/prometheus/rules/nora.yml`, with the two counters created at zero at start for every platform (`prime_delete_metrics`) and promtool cases that start the series absent; one central guard re-reads the row's hidden state before any downstream stage (a failed read is asked again, twice stops the message with its own outcome) and closes only the window between the audit write and that read; writers lock the cited messages, sorted ascending, before their own row, the curator's batch once for the whole batch, and `person forget` locks its hide in ascending id order (pinned by a forced interleaving in both directions). **(2) Which stores (orchestrator's decision, for the operator to confirm):** a delete withdraws notes, events and the `pending` and `refused` `note_candidate` proposals read off the message (deleted), and does NOT mark Standing or culture: their citation is a fold WATERMARK (`last_folded_row_id`, the room's newest message), edges accumulate across revisions, so one ordinary delete of any former fold boundary hid the CURRENT head permanently while a delete mid-fold left it standing; they re-fold from the live transcript, which no longer holds the message. Residual: a fold keeps a deleted message's content in its own raw prior until it rewrites it. `person forget` is unchanged. **(3) Who may delete:** Signal and WhatsApp only the author (`nora.domain.delete_authorship`: the id, the person, or any id form the event carries), anyone else `refused_not_author`, at ingest, when a kept delete is applied, in the start-up sweep over records written before the rule existed, and in `unforget`; the WhatsApp bridge forwards any REVOKE (end-to-end encrypted) with the revoker in the event, and a group admin's removal is NOT honoured (the message stays visible). Discord and Instagram name no deleter and are the platform's word. **(4) Honcho cannot forget** (no per-message delete): text it already read may remain; nothing in Nora feeds a hidden row again, and the comprehension job asks whether its message is withdrawn before the vision call and the feed. **(5) A deleted message stays hidden:** `unforget` leaves it hidden (`kept_deleted`), and a head the cascade marked stays withdrawn. **This holds unless** the operator rules that a delete should mark Standing and culture (then the watermark must become real evidence first, or heads must be able to recover), or that a WhatsApp admin removal should be honoured (then group metadata must reach Python). | `tests/unit/test_ingest_stimuli.py::test_a_delete_is_recorded_and_raises_a_stimulus`, `tests/infra/test_withdrawal.py::test_hide_message_hides_a_row_once_and_a_snapshot_before_it_restores_the_row` |

(2) `ReplyGuard._after_tool` ends the turn (`_turn_is_over`, the same cancel-first path as the budget cap, so DEC-93's `cancelled_model_call` stays set and the cancel text is never recovered as her prose) when the call's own result is `sent` or `held_for_review` and `more` is not true. (3) A `refused` result (R-6, R-18, an audit or send failure) and a result the guard cannot read keep today's relaxed path, so she can still retry; a call the guard vetoed or that raised never reached this branch. (4) The budget stays 3 (DEC-42, 2026-09-22), `send_gif` is unchanged (its budget of 1 already ends the turn), summons has a budget of 1 so it ends after its send either way and `more` and `heads_up` are inert there, and every path that builds a `ReplyGuard` (tag, participation, proactive, summons, the fire shadows) gets the same behaviour because they share one guard; Cognition and the Dreamer use `DreamGuard`, which has no terminal verb. (5) UNMEASURED: whether `more` is passed when a second message is wanted; the reply-shape evals and the multi-message rate on live traces (4 of 45 recent turns used the relaxed call before) are what would show a loss. (6) Operator 2026-10-09, «she decides»: before work that will keep the room waiting, of any kind, she sends one short line of what she is about to do, marked `heads_up=true` on `send_reply` (which keeps the turn open like `more`), then the work, then the answer (`conduct.md` v35, «Getting to an answer», which names no tool; a quick check still gets no filler). That heads-up is delivered, so `ReplyGuard.reply_still_owed` (her last landed send carried `heads_up`) re-opens DEC-93's recovery, the salvage and the cut-off fallback for its answer (`pipeline._nothing_answered`); before it, a prose answer after a heads-up was dropped while the turn read as `replied`. Her flag, not an inference: «a `more=true` send, then work» could not tell a heads-up from an answer followed by a note, after which closing prose would have reached the room. Eval 2026-10-09, `tool_selection` 16 cases n=3, measured under `more` before `heads_up` existed: a heads-up line in 2 long-work draws, 0 on quick controls; model calls 286 to 261. Whether she sets `heads_up` on such a line is measured separately (PR #754). | DEC-305 | **Nora makes short video clips with `video_create`: MiniMax CN, `MiniMax-H3`, 480P, 15 s, an explicit ratio (default 3:4), optional reference images, a hard daily cap per room, shipped `[video_gen] enabled = false`.** Operator 2026-10-02 (design/video-generation/00-design.md §2, built §9). The clip is a deferred job in the compute outbox (kind `video`): the tool starts it and returns, `ComputeJobPoller` delivers the finished clip as a LINK (the signed URL, valid 24 h, attached to her message by code, §6 option 1, because the deploy host cannot reach mainland Aliyun storage). The cap (`max_clips_per_room_per_day`, per room and local day) is checked in code before every create and counted from `compute_jobs`, so a restart never resets it; a clip the provider failed does not count. **Amended 2026-10-09 (operator): the cap is per ROOM (platform plus conversation id), each room may start that many clips per local day; it counted every room together before.** The key was renamed from `max_clips_per_day` so the name says what it counts, and the old key is refused at load with a message naming the new one (a deployment's `config.toml` must change it in the same deploy); the refusal note says it is this room's limit. **Amended 2026-10-10 (operator): a finished clip is downloaded, kept in her media library (blob store and a `generated` media_objects row, like `generate_image`) and sent to the room as a video attachment; the provider link is no longer shown.** The link premise is withdrawn on a read-back: from inside the nora container on norty the signed Aliyun URL downloaded 7.5 MB with an `ftyp` header in 1.2 s (2026-10-10). The download waits until the room's slot is held, is capped (50 MB, 120 s, MP4 only), retries on later ticks until 15 minutes after launch and then falls back to the link; a too-large or non-MP4 answer falls back at once. The `httpx` log line drops URL query strings so the signature never reaches a log. A platform that rejects the attachment fails that send with no link fallback. This part holds unless the storage host stops answering from norty. **Amended 2026-10-10 (operator): `video_create` also takes `first_frame`, one held photo that opens the clip (image-to-video, role `first_frame`, ratio `adaptive` for that mode only), mutually exclusive with references and behind the same `allow_reference_images` gate.** A photo the requester wants to move is the first frame; a new scene with the same subject stays reference mode. `last_frame` is not built. One lock still serves all rooms. A reference is a photo she holds (this conversation's, or her canonical picture), sent as a `data:` URI, never an external URL, and only under `allow_reference_images` (default off). `ratio = "adaptive"` is refused at load (the live API refused it for a reference task), and so is `enabled` without `[compute] enabled`. A video row survives a restart (its handle is the provider's task id); boot recovery still sweeps an in-memory sub-agent row. Not in scope: other resolutions or durations, editing. **Amended 2026-10-10 (operator): a reference may also be a clip or a voice note held in this conversation, told apart by the held blob's media type (the same three `reference` slots, no new argument), each kind behind its own gate (`allow_reference_video`, `allow_reference_audio`, both default off) and fitted with ffmpeg before the create.** The provider refuses an out-of-range reference only at the poll (a 12 fps clip, an `audio/mpeg` URI, measured 2026-10-10), so every clip is cut, cropped into aspect 0.4 to 2.5, scaled, clamped to 24 to 30 fps and re-encoded H.264 with AAC, every sound becomes a mono MP3 sent as `data:audio/mp3`, metadata stripped, and a reference under 2 s is refused, never padded. `reference_seconds` (default 6, 6 to 15) is shared by the references of each kind; a clip's seconds are billed beside the output's and audio was not (measured 2026-10-10, one 4 s render each). A first frame stays a photo. This part holds unless the provider changes its reference limits. This holds unless the first live 15 s clip is refused for H3 (then `model = "MiniMax-H3-Max"`, a config change inside this decision) or its measured cost moves the cap. | | DEC-306 | **The memo kind is built: what a unit SETTLED and will need again is kept as a memo, written only by the Cognition session, read through `<memos>` and `memo_read`.** Operator 2026-10-09 (design/cognition-loop/40-register.md §1-§2, 12-schemas.md §3, migration step 7 / E1b; amends DEC-226, DEC-230 and DEC-281, marked there). (1) **The routing rule**: settled and about the speaker alone is `remember`'s (Memory); settled and about the unit, someone else or the world is a memo; not settled is a note; dated and attended is an event. A memo never closes: `memo_revise` restates it whole on its head (`stale_base` otherwise) and `memo_withdraw` ends it only on a cited message saying it no longer holds; a second kept memo under one title is refused `duplicate`, naming the first. (2) **Store**: `memo` and `memo_revision` (migration `0103_memos`), the lesson's shape (DEC-293): an identity per unit with its origin room, and an append-only chain whose revisions carry title, body, citations, mode (`told`, `deduced`, `abduced`), state (`kept`, `withdrawn`), `cognition:<unit>` and the model; no generic entry store, no `about` or `links`. The withdrawn state is a revision, not an identity column, so both tables stay append-only (`history.APPEND_ONLY`). (3) **Body**: `## Kept` (required) and `## Conditions`, every line ending in the ids it rests on (the note body's line grammar, `nora.domain.memo.parse_memo_body`); `## Superseded` is rendered by `memo_read` from the chain and refused when a model writes it (`code_written`). (4) **Content (D5)**: a Kept line holds anything said, verbatim, a password, number or booking reference included; the session's identifier screen reads the title and `## Conditions` and never a Kept line (DEC-230), and R-18 still refuses a key-shaped value read from a memo in a reply (DEC-226). (5) **Own sends**: a memo line MAY cite Nora's own message, so «記低» of something she found is kept with the person's message asking for it; a note still refuses `cites_nora`. (6) **Visibility**: `<memos>` (titles, ids, updated day; never a Kept line) renders unit-wide in every room of the unit on the tag, fire and Cognition prompts like `<notes>`, absent when nothing is kept; no R-31 restriction. (7) **Who decides**: a session may write a memo whenever something the unit will need again is settled, «記低» or not; most settles need none; a note closing settled may leave one. The tag turn writes nothing: it says the thing WILL be kept, and `keep` re-arms a strong-cue wake (DEC-281 amended). (8) One integrated change, no shadow week, no config key (only a session writes, and with none kept every read renders nothing). (9) **Review of #781, same day**: a title names the thing and never carries a value a Kept line keeps (refused `title_carries_value`: an alphanumeric run of 4+ characters with a digit shared with a Kept line); a person's explicit ask to keep something about the group is written, not weighed, unless it is about the speaker alone or still open; a withdrawn head is final in both stores; `<memos>` is capped at 20 rows and 1,200 characters, newest first, with `not_listed`, on every prompt, and in the Cognition prompt it has its own budget after the events; the keep cue also matches 記住 and «remember this/that», never 記住啦你 banter; the tag turn says it will note it down, naming no time. | DEC-308 | **Every OAuth login Nora generates media with is refreshed by the daemon on a schedule, not only when a call needs it: one generic keepalive (`nora.app.oauth_keepalive`) that any OAuth lane registers with, at least once per `refresh_interval_hours` (default 24) and before the access token expires; both image lanes share one rotating-refresh-token chain (`nora.infra.image_gen.oauth_lane`).** Operator 2026-10-09: «Both xAI and Codex must refresh their tokens proactively, NOT lazily — I should not have to log in again every time», refined the same day to every OAuth provider for image or video, «daily or bi-daily». Evidence: the xAI lane's last refresh was 2026-09-27; the first call on 2026-10-09 got `invalid_grant` for the stored rotated token, and the failure logged nothing. (1) Registrants today are `xai` and `openai_codex`, each kept whenever `[image_gen] enabled` and its token env var is set, WHICHEVER `provider` is selected; `keepalive = false` opts a lane out. A future OAuth video provider registers the same way; MiniMax CN (`video_create`, DEC-305) authenticates with an API key and has no login to keep. (2) The keeper refreshes through the lane's own `refresh`, which takes the same asyncio lock and host `flock` as a `generate_image` call and adopts any link minted after it planned, so the keeper and a call never both spend a rotating token. (3) Transient failures (`down`, `rate_limited`, `cloudflare`) back off 1 min doubling to 30 min; a terminal one (`auth`, `state_unwritable`) is retried once per interval and logged at ERROR each time; a crashed loop is logged with its traceback, counted, and restarted. (4) Every refresh failure, from the keeper or a call, logs its lane and reason, never the token. Gauges `nora_oauth_last_refresh_timestamp_seconds`, `nora_oauth_access_expiry_timestamp_seconds` and `nora_oauth_refresh_interval_seconds` (republished at boot from the state file), `nora_oauth_refresh_refused` (set by each outcome, including a rotation that could not be written), and the counter `nora_oauth_refresh_failures_total`; alerts `OAuthRefreshStale` (no success for twice the interval, on the timestamp, never a rare counter), `OAuthAccessTokenExpired` (an expired access token for 30 min) and `OAuthRefreshRefused`. A pre-fingerprint chain is retired in favour of the `.env` login only on a dead-token error code (`invalid_grant` and kin), and a 403 without one is transient. (5) The xAI state file is fingerprinted to its `.env` bootstrap token like the Codex one (DEC-304 (2)), with the same cross-process lock and fail-closed persistence: a fresh `nora xai-login` supersedes a dead chain without deleting a file. A state file written before this has no fingerprint: its token is tried once (it may be the live chain, the `.env` token already spent by the old code) and the `.env` login is spent only if the issuer refuses it; either way the file is rewritten with the fingerprint. (6) The daemon starts the keeper (`nora/__main__.py`); the eval subject composes the same graph and does not start it. A `generate_image` case in an eval run on the host still builds lanes at `/app/state`, which is not writable there, so it answers `state_unwritable` and spends nothing (fail-closed); before this the xAI lane refreshed without that check, which makes an eval run one candidate second holder of the 2026-10-09 token. Not in scope: the cause of the 2026-10-09 refusal (idle expiry, or revocation by a second holder of the same bootstrap token in another checkout's `.env`), which only a live login can tell. This holds unless a lane's issuer limits refreshes per day below one per interval, or a refresh is shown to shorten a refresh token's life. | `tests/contract/test_oauth_lane_contract.py::test_the_keeper_refreshes_on_the_interval_with_no_calls`, `tests/contract/test_oauth_lane_contract.py::test_the_keeper_refreshes_before_the_access_token_expires`, `tests/contract/test_oauth_lane_contract.py::test_the_keeper_and_live_calls_spend_the_token_once`, `tests/contract/test_oauth_lane_contract.py::test_a_fresh_login_supersedes_a_dead_chain_in_the_state_file`, `tests/contract/test_oauth_lane_contract.py::test_a_refused_refresh_is_logged_with_its_lane_and_never_its_token`, `tests/unit/test_oauth_keepalive.py::test_a_terminal_failure_stops_hammering_and_stays_loud`, `tests/unit/test_oauth_keepalive.py::test_a_crash_is_logged_counted_and_the_loop_restarted`, `tests/unit/test_oauth_keepalive.py::test_every_lane_with_a_token_is_kept_whichever_provider_is_selected`, `tests/unit/test_oauth_alert_rules.py::test_the_oauth_rules_pass_their_promtool_cases` |

| DEC-313 | **A memory index read reaches only the reading room's scope, checked on every node of every path, and never fans out through a hub.** Operator ruling 2026-10-15 (`design/unified-memory/25-memory-graph.md` §4 step 1 and 3, `35-persona.md` §3, `60-build-step-3.md` §0.1, §0.3 and S5). The scope is computed per read from the live policy and the room's live roster: a node is in scope when it is `live` and belongs to the room's unit or one of that unit's rooms (or, for a stay or trip, which carry neither, to a person), every person it is readable only to is listed in the room, it names nobody excluded who is here (any exclusion when the room cannot vouch for who is in it), and an outing, stay or trip only where every person of it passes presence there (the room's `location` flag and the live DisclosureGuard, R-31, DEC-222). A person, room, unit, Nora or place node carries no scope: it is returned only as a direct neighbour, never seeds and never joins the next hop's frontier. An edge to person P is followed only if the reading room lists P and the node it leaves was said in a room that lists P. Lineage mode is not consulted (it stays off). Read by `ask_memory` (since DEC-316, `memory_search`, the only verb on the graph surface) only while `[memory_index] enabled` (ships off). | DEC-315 | **`ask_memory` (since DEC-316 `memory_search`) seeds from the question's vector and pins literal references ahead of it; the trigram seed is only the fallback, and a fallback answer is `partial`.** Operator 2026-10-16 (`design/unified-memory/65-build-step-3-vectors.md` V2, §4; `25-memory-graph.md` §4 step 2). While `[memory_index] enabled` and `embed` (both ship off), the question is embedded once with the model's query instruction, and the dense seed takes the 50 nearest by the leading 256 dimensions through the HNSW index with the scope filter and the model fingerprint inside the scan (`hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order`, `hnsw.ef_search = 100`), re-scored by full 2048 cosine; a vector of another model is never compared. An **exact** seed is a node containing, literally, a URL, a handle or an id-like token (six or more digits, or five or more letters and digits with a letter and at least three digits, never a time, ordinal or measure), in any case, or a name of a person the reading room lists (the name Nora calls them, first name, full name or alias, never the bare last name nor a name that is also a common word), as written, in the NFKC-normalised question (`nora.agent.memory_search.exact_terms_of`); an ordinary word never is. A Latin term matches as a whole word, any other script as a substring. The first five exact hits (`PINNED_LIMIT`, half the answer) rank ahead of every other hit, however near («a literal name match must not lose to a near-duplicate»); the rest rank by their cosine, so half the answer always goes by score (amended 2026-10-16 after the review of #31: ten pinned hits had filled every slot). The lexical seed runs when there is no query vector (`embed` off, the embedder failed, or no node in scope holds a current vector yet), and that answer is `partial`, never `nothing_found`; so is any answer while live embeddable nodes in the search's scope wait for a current vector, except those the worker gave up on, which the lexical seed reads beside the dense one, and attachments that failed as `empty`. **Amended 2026-10-17 (found building the eval harness, #54): a fresh wait is not a backlog.** The lexical seed beside the dense one reads every embeddable node in scope holding no current vector, waiting or given up, so a line said a moment ago is found by its words; only a node that has owed its vector longer than `BACKLOG_TICKS` (3) drain periods (`[memory_index] drain_seconds`, measured from `memory_node.owed_since`, migration 0111, reset only when the embedded input changes) holds the answer `partial`, as does any waiting or given-up node when the question has no search terms; an attachment with no text is never fresh, since nothing reads it until its vector lands (`design/unified-memory/65-build-step-3-vectors.md` §4.5). **The trade, accepted:** for up to three periods a fresh line is reachable only by shared words, so a reworded question about it can answer `nothing_found`. Acceptable because a line said within the last ~3 minutes is in the turn's own visible transcript, which she reads before any search; the alternative held almost every live answer `partial`. Only a failure of the input itself counts toward the worker's give-up cap; an unavailable embedder never does. `hnsw.max_scan_tuples = 50000`, and a short dense scan is counted (`nora_memory_dense_short_total`). The relevance floor is unchanged (0.1 of cosine), so a dense search returns its nearest even when nothing is relevant; the floor, and the `about` seed's fixed 0.6, are calibrated in V3. This holds unless V3's `conversational_recall` run loses a case the lexical seed found, or a pinned literal is measured crowding out the answer. | `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_an_exact_name_outranks_a_closer_dense_neighbour`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_embedder_down_answers_partial_with_lexical_results`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_the_scan_keeps_going_past_out_of_scope_neighbours`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_the_planner_scans_the_hnsw_index_with_the_scope_inside`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_a_vector_of_another_model_is_never_compared`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_a_backlog_keeps_it_partial_and_given_up_ones_are_read_by_their_words`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_a_line_just_said_is_found_by_its_words_and_the_answer_is_ok`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_literal_hits_hold_half_the_answer_and_a_cosine_one_hit_still_shows`, `tests/integration/test_memory_dense_seed.py::test_a_node_waiting_in_another_unit_does_not_make_this_room_partial`, `tests/integration/test_memory_vectors.py::test_an_unavailable_embedder_never_gives_a_node_up`, `tests/unit/test_memory_search.py::test_exact_terms_are_literal_references_never_ordinary_words` |
| DEC-316 | **`[memory_index] enabled` selects ONE memory tool surface, the memory graph's or Honcho's, never both; on the graph surface the one search verb is `memory_search(query, person?, since?, until?, kinds?)`, with no Honcho behind it.** Operator rulings 2026-10-16 (`design/unified-memory/60-build-step-3.md` §0.7, a person-free single verb; and the correction of PR #32: Honcho and the graph never coexist on a surface, after a `tool_selection` run with `memory_search` beside Honcho's `search_memory` called `search_memory` in 6 of 8 new cases and `memory_search` in none, n=1, ADR 0004's near-name pattern). **The flag is the surface.** Off (the default, production, the rollback): exactly the Honcho surface before this decision, `ask_memory`, `search_memory`, `search_memory_workspace` and `who_said`, and no `memory_search`. On: `memory_search`, and none of those four. **Amended 2026-10-17 (operator ruling, option a): the graph surface holds no Honcho tool at all.** `about` (the profile read) and `remember` (the person-fact write) read and write Honcho, so they are on the Honcho surface alone (`HONCHO_MEMORY_TOOLS`); a profile question on the graph surface is `memory_search` with `person`, and the graph surface has no person-fact write verb until Persona (unified-memory steps 5-8) and step 9 give it one (`note_create` keeps an open question, not a settled fact). `load_transcript` (the in-room scroll-back) reads the room's own rows and is on both. `who_said` is deprecated: the graph surface does without it, because `memory_search` names who said each hit and `load_transcript` reads around it; it is deleted with the rest of the Honcho surface at step 9. The selection is made once, in `build_tool_specs`, the builder every assembly point takes tools from (a tag, a fire turn, the Cognition session, every Dreamer adaptor, the sub-agent worker), from whether the registry holds a `MemorySearch` (`nora.agent.tools.HONCHO_MEMORY_TOOLS`, `GRAPH_MEMORY_TOOLS`). The registry is the ONE source: it also withholds the unselected surface (`ToolRegistry.withheld_tools()`), so the capability digest names one surface, and the Cognition session's `read_surface` takes that set as a required argument rather than re-deriving the flag from config. The sub-agent worker holds no `memory_search`: it reads the unit's other rooms, which the worker's one-room reach refuses (design/subagent §4c), as it refused `search_memory_workspace`. `memory_search` holds `search_memory`'s resident slot under deferral (`HOT_TOOLS`), and R-91's ration counts every memory verb of both surfaces. `ask_memory` lost its index branch: it is never built with the index on. **The verb.** Named `<domain>_<verb>` (ADR 0015); a new tool beside the Honcho ones, so nothing moves to `_RENAMED_SINCE`. `kinds` is a `Literal` of five plain categories over the node kinds (`nora.domain.memory_index.KINDS_BY_CATEGORY`: messages, media, notes = note, memo, lesson and Character account, events, places = outing, stay and trip); `since` and `until` are ISO dates, a bare date the start or the end of that day at the fixed UTC+8 offset `_parse_when` uses; a bad date, a span that ends before it starts or an unknown kind is `unavailable` with a note. `person`, `since` and `until` are a `MemoryFilter` on the scope (`MemoryScope.only`), ANDed onto DEC-313's filter inside every read (the HNSW scan, the exact and lexical seeds, the `about` seeds, every hop, the coverage count), so a node outside them is never read, never returned and never takes a slot; a person narrows to nodes with an `about`, `authored_by` or `shared_by` edge to them or listing them in `persons`, under the listed-room rule. `kinds` narrows the seeds and the answer, not the hops: the seeds run once with it and once without, the hops cross any kind, and only the asked kinds are ranked and returned, because an outing, stay or trip has no vector and is reached from what was said during it. A person the live roster resolves but this room's policy does not list, or any person in a `*` room, is `unavailable` with a note before any read, never a false `nothing_found`. **Reach per occasion (coordinator ruling 2026-10-16):** the culture adaptor's `memory_search` reads its OWN room alone (`ROOM_ONLY_MEMORY_ADAPTORS`, `scope_for(own_room=True)`: no other room of the unit and no unit-placed node, the listed-room and presence rules unchanged), because a room's culture must not be written from another room's speech, and its Honcho `search_memory` read only its own session; every other occasion, the character-person session included, reads the unit under the listed-room rule, no wider than `ask_memory` over the index was on origin/master. The routing measurement is `python -m evals tool_selection --memory-index` against the deployment's Honcho surface; the run resolves its surface from the generated config's `[memory_index] enabled` or the flag, prints it, and refuses a case whose composed subject is on the other surface; cases that route on one surface only say so (`metadata.memory_surface`). This holds unless the graph arm of that run shows `memory_search` losing the memory routes the Honcho arm wins (the profile question included: `about` on the Honcho arm, `memory_search` with `person` on the graph arm), or taking routes from `where_been`, `media_search` or `lookup_person`. | `tests/unit/test_memory_surfaces.py::test_the_graph_surface_offers_memory_search_and_no_honcho_memory_verb`, `tests/unit/test_memory_surfaces.py::test_the_honcho_surface_is_origin_masters_with_no_memory_search`, `tests/unit/test_memory_search_tool.py::test_on_an_out_of_window_node_is_never_returned_and_takes_no_slot`, `tests/unit/test_memory_search_tool.py::test_on_a_person_the_room_does_not_list_is_unavailable_not_nothing`, `tests/unit/test_memory_search.py::test_kinds_narrow_the_answer_not_the_hops_so_an_outing_is_reached`, `tests/unit/test_memory_search_tool.py::test_a_culture_pass_never_reads_another_rooms_line`, `tests/test_composition.py::test_cognition_holds_the_memory_surface_the_flag_selects`, `tests/contract/test_memory_index_contract.py` (the narrowing cases), `tests/unit/test_eval_scenarios.py::test_each_arm_runs_only_the_cases_its_memory_surface_can_route` |
